<h2>What are Meshery Models and Components?</h2>

<p>Meshery Models and Components represent the fundamental building blocks of your infrastructure. Use them to define the structure and configuration of your infrastructure and deployments by incorporating their use into a Design. Think of Designs as blueprints or templates that encapsulate everything from network configurations to service definitions.</p>

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>, and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a></h6>

<h2>What is the Meshery Registry</h2>

The Meshery Registry is a vital component within Meshery, serving as a centralized repository for managing a diverse range of cloud and cloud native resources. It stores and organizes crucial information such as models, categories, components, and relationships, enabling efficient interaction and utilization of these resources within the Meshery ecosystem. You can conveniently access and manage registry data through Meshery UI, and through Meshery CLI (<a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/registry">mesheryctl registry</a>).

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a></h6>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<h2>What are Meshery Models and Components?</h2>

<p>Meshery Models and Components represent the fundamental building blocks of your infrastructure. Use them to define the structure and configuration of your infrastructure and deployments by incorporating their use into a Design. Think of Designs as blueprints or templates that encapsulate everything from network configurations to service definitions.</p>

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>, and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a></h6>

<h2>What is the Meshery Registry</h2>

The Meshery Registry is a vital component within Meshery, serving as a centralized repository for managing a diverse range of cloud and cloud native resources. It stores and organizes crucial information such as models, categories, components, and relationships, enabling efficient interaction and utilization of these resources within the Meshery ecosystem. You can conveniently access and manage registry data through Meshery UI, and through Meshery CLI (<a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/registry">mesheryctl registry</a>).

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a></h6>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<h2>What are Meshery Models and Components?</h2>

<p>Meshery Models and Components represent the fundamental building blocks of your infrastructure. Use them to define the structure and configuration of your infrastructure and deployments by incorporating their use into a Design. Think of Designs as blueprints or templates that encapsulate everything from network configurations to service definitions.</p>

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>, and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a></h6>

<h2>What is the Meshery Registry</h2>

The Meshery Registry is a vital component within Meshery, serving as a centralized repository for managing a diverse range of cloud and cloud native resources. It stores and organizes crucial information such as models, categories, components, and relationships, enabling efficient interaction and utilization of these resources within the Meshery ecosystem. You can conveniently access and manage registry data through Meshery UI, and through Meshery CLI (<a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/registry">mesheryctl registry</a>).

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a></h6>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<h2>What are Meshery Models and Components?</h2>

<p>Meshery Models and Components represent the fundamental building blocks of your infrastructure. Use them to define the structure and configuration of your infrastructure and deployments by incorporating their use into a Design. Think of Designs as blueprints or templates that encapsulate everything from network configurations to service definitions.</p>

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>, and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a></h6>

<h2>What is the Meshery Registry</h2>

The Meshery Registry is a vital component within Meshery, serving as a centralized repository for managing a diverse range of cloud and cloud native resources. It stores and organizes crucial information such as models, categories, components, and relationships, enabling efficient interaction and utilization of these resources within the Meshery ecosystem. You can conveniently access and manage registry data through Meshery UI, and through Meshery CLI (<a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/registry">mesheryctl registry</a>).

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a></h6>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<!-- <a href="http://idratherbewriting.com" class="noCrossRef productSubtitle"> Home </a> > <a class="noCrossRef productSubtitle" href="https://docs.meshery.io">Learn API Doc</a> > load-generators -->

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Extensibility: Load Generators</h1>
           <p>Users may prefer to use one load generator over the next given the difference of capabilities between load generators, so Meshery provides a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">load generator interface</code> (a gRPC interface) behind which a load generator can be implemented. Meshery provides users with choice of which load generator they prefer to use for a given performance test. Users may configure their own preference for the load generator, different from the default load generator.</p>

<h3 id="what-function-do-load-generators-in-meshery-provide">What function do load generators in Meshery provide?</h3>

<p>Load generators will provide the capability to run load tests from Meshery. As of today the load generators are embedded as libraries in Meshery and Meshery invokes the load generators APIs with the right load test options to run the load test. At the moment, Meshery supports HTTP load generation. Support for gRPC and TCP load generation is on the roadmap. Meshery has functional integration with fortio, wrk2, and nighthawk.</p>

<h3 id="why-support-multiple-load-generators">Why support multiple load generators?</h3>

<p>Different use cases and different opinions call for different approaches to statistical analysis of the performance results. For example, wrk2 accounts for a concept called Coordinated Omission.</p>

<h3 id="which-load-generators-does-meshery-support">Which load generators does Meshery support?</h3>

<ol>
  <li><a href="https://github.com/fortio/fortio">fortio</a> - Fortio load testing library, command line tool, advanced echo server and web UI in go (golang). Allows to specify a set query-per-second load and record latency histograms and other useful stats.</li>
  <li><a href="https://github.com/giltene/wrk2">wrk2</a> - A constant throughput, correct latency recording variant of wrk.</li>
  <li><a href="https://getnighthawk.dev/">nighthawk</a> - Enables users to run distributed performance tests to better mimic real-world, distributed systems scenarios.
    <ul>
      <li>See the Nighthawk project.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>
   <br/>

        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link

        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({

          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });

<!-- <a href="http://idratherbewriting.com" class="noCrossRef productSubtitle"> Home </a> > <a class="noCrossRef productSubtitle" href="https://docs.meshery.io">Learn API Doc</a> > providers -->

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Extensibility: Providers</h1>
           <p>Meshery offers <em>Providers</em> as a point of extensibility. It has a built-in Local Provider, named <strong>“None”</strong> and supports <em>Remote Providers</em> that are designed to be pluggable. <em>Remote Providers</em> offer a point of extension to users / integrators to deliver enhanced functionality such as authentication and authorization, using Meshery as a platform.</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Extensibility points offer clean separation of Meshery’s core functionality versus plugin functionality.</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>See a list of <a href="https://meshery.io/extensions">Meshery’s extensions</a>.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Remote Providers should be able to offer custom RBAC, custom UI components, and custom backend components</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Dynamically loadable frameworks need to be identified or created to serve each of these purposes.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<h3 id="what-functionality-do-providers-offer">What functionality do Providers offer?</h3>

<p>The functionalities offerred by a <em>Remote Provider</em> may vary broadly between providers. Meshery offers extension points that Remote Providers are able to use to inject various functionalities, functionalities that are specific to that provider.
Some examples include:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Authentication and Authorization</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Examples: session management, two factor authentication, LDAP integration.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Long-Term Persistence</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Examples: Storage and retrieval of performance test results.</li>
      <li>Examples: Storage and retrieval of user preferences.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Enhanced Visualization</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Examples: Creation of a visual cloud native infrastructure topology.</li>
      <li>Examples: Different charts (metrics), debug (log viewer), distributed trace explorers.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Reporting</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Examples: Using Meshery’s GraphQL server to compose new dashboards.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Server Event Management</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Examples: Local event storage in database</li>
      <li>Examples: Remote event synchronization (Remote providers only)</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/providers/providers.png">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/providers/providers.png" width="50%" /></a></p>

<figcaption>Figure: Selecting a provider in Meshery</figcaption>

<h2 id="types-of-providers">Types of providers</h2>

<p>There are two types of providers defined in Meshery, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">local</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">remote</code>.</p>

<ul>
  <li>The <strong>Local</strong> provider is built-into Meshery.</li>
  <li><strong>Remote providers</strong> can be implemented by anyone or an organization that wishes to integrate with Meshery. Any number of Remote providers may be available in your Meshery deployment.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="default-installation-configuration">Default Installation Configuration</h3>

<p>By default, Meshery installations <strong>do not have a provider preselected</strong>. This is an intentional design choice: upon first launch, users are presented with the provider selection UI, allowing them to make an informed choice among all available providers.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Why no default provider?</h4>
It might be tempting to preselect the Local provider ("None") as the default; however, doing so would preclude selection of any other provider by new users who are unaware of other options being available. By leaving the provider unset, all users (whether individual or team-based) are presented with the full range of available providers on first use.
</div>

<h3 id="recommended-production-deployment-settings">Recommended Production Deployment Settings</h3>

<p>For production deployments, consider the following security best practices regarding provider selection:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Do not pre-select a provider</strong> in the default installation configuration. Allow users to choose their provider at startup.</li>
  <li><strong>Use a Remote Provider</strong> for production deployments to enforce user authentication and authorization, especially for public-facing Meshery instances.</li>
  <li><strong>Enforce a specific provider</strong> using the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER</code> environment variable only when you have a clear operational requirement to do so, such as locking a deployment to a particular identity provider.</li>
  <li><strong>Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system provider set</code></strong> to explicitly configure a provider for a given context when needed.</li>
  <li><strong>Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system provider reset</code></strong> to clear an enforced provider and return to the provider selection UI.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="remote-providers">Remote Providers</h3>

<p>The use of a Remote Provider, puts Meshery into multi-user mode and requires user authentication. This provides security for the public-facing Meshery UI as the remote provider enforces identity with authentication and authorization. You should also use a remote provider when your use of Meshery is ongoing or used in a team environment (used by multiple people). This can be seen when using Meshery Playground, where a user is prompted to login through the <em>Meshery Cloud</em> remote provider. Visit <a href="https://playground.meshery.io/">Meshery Playground</a> to experience this.</p>

<p>A specific provider can be enforced in a Meshery instance by passing the name of the provider with the env variable <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER</code>. This applies to both remote and local providers.</p>

<p>Name: <strong>"Meshery"</strong> (default)</p>

<ul>
  <li>Enforces user authentication.</li>
  <li>Long-term term persistence.</li>
  <li>Save environment setup.</li>
  <li>Retrieve performance test results.</li>
  <li>Events are stored locally and can be published to remote provider. <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-server-events">Read more about server events</a></li>
</ul>

<h4 id="example-remote-provider">Example remote provider</h4>

<p>Name: <strong>“Acme”</strong> (default)</p>

<ul>
  <li>Enforces user authentication.</li>
  <li>Long-term term persistence.</li>
  <li>Save environment setup.</li>
  <li>Retrieve performance test results.</li>
  <li>Events are stored locally and can be published to remote provider. <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-server-events">Read more about server events</a></li>
  <li>Free to use.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="local-provider">Local Provider</h3>

<p>The use of the Local Provider, <strong>“None”</strong>, puts Meshery into a single-user mode and does not require authentication. Use the Local provider when your use of Meshery is intended to be shortlived.</p>

<p>Name: <strong>“None”</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>No user authentication.</li>
  <li>Immediate login - users are redirected directly to the dashboard without authentication prompts.</li>
  <li>Container-local storage of test results. Ephemeral.</li>
  <li>Environment setup not saved.</li>
  <li>No performance test result history.</li>
  <li>Server events are stored locally in database. <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-server-events">Read more about server events</a></li>
  <li>Free to use.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="login-behavior">Login Behavior</h4>

<p>When the Local Provider is selected, users are immediately redirected to the Meshery dashboard without any authentication challenges. The login flow for <strong>“None”</strong> provider:</p>

<ol>
  <li>User selects <strong>“None”</strong> provider from the provider selection UI (or it’s enforced via <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER</code> environment variable)</li>
  <li>The provider cookie is set and user is redirected to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/user/login</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">InitiateLogin</code> immediately redirects to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/</code> (dashboard) or to the originally requested page if a deep-link was preserved</li>
  <li>User begins working with Meshery without any authentication barriers</li>
</ol>

<p>This streamlined flow makes the Local Provider ideal for quick evaluations, demos, and single-user scenarios where authentication overhead is unnecessary.</p>

<h2 id="provider-login-flow">Provider Login Flow</h2>

<p>Understanding how provider selection leads to authentication and dashboard access is important for both users and integrators.</p>

<h3 id="interactive-browser-flow">Interactive (Browser) Flow</h3>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Provider Selection</strong>: User visits Meshery and is presented with the provider selection UI at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/provider</code> (unless a provider is enforced via the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER</code> environment variable)</li>
  <li><strong>Provider Activation</strong>: User selects a provider → Meshery sets a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery-provider</code> cookie and redirects to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/user/login?provider=&lt;name&gt;</code></li>
  <li><strong>Login Initiation</strong>: The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/user/login</code> route resolves the provider and calls the provider’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">InitiateLogin</code> method:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>For “None” (Local)</strong>: Immediately redirects to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/</code> (dashboard) or to the deep-link target if one was preserved</li>
      <li><strong>For Remote Providers</strong>: Redirects to the remote provider’s OAuth login page (e.g., GitHub, Google)</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Post-Authentication</strong>: After successful authentication, user is redirected to the dashboard or originally requested page</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="enforced-provider-flow">Enforced Provider Flow</h3>

<p>When the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER</code> environment variable is set (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER=None</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER=Meshery</code>):</p>

<ol>
  <li>Provider selection UI is bypassed</li>
  <li>The specified provider is automatically activated and cookie is set</li>
  <li>User is redirected directly to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/user/login</code></li>
  <li>Login flow proceeds as described above based on provider type</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="deep-link-preservation">Deep-Link Preservation</h3>

<p>Meshery preserves the originally requested URL when authentication is required, enabling seamless navigation after login:</p>

<ul>
  <li>When an unauthenticated user attempts to access a protected page, the URL is base64-encoded into a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ref</code> query parameter</li>
  <li>After successful login, the provider decodes <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ref</code> and redirects to the original destination</li>
  <li>The Local Provider supports this functionality, validating <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ref</code> values to prevent open redirects (absolute URLs, protocol-relative URLs, and URLs with schemes/hosts are rejected)</li>
  <li>If <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ref</code> validation fails or is absent, users are redirected to the dashboard (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/</code>)</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Example</strong>: User visits <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">https://meshery.example.com/extension/meshmap</code> while unauthenticated → redirected to login with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ref</code> parameter → after login, automatically returned to MeshMap extension.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Deep-Link Security</h4>
Deep-link targets are validated to prevent open redirect vulnerabilities. Only relative paths within the Meshery application are accepted.
</div>

<h2 id="runtime-configuration-options">Runtime Configuration Options</h2>

<p>Meshery provides runtime configuration options to control provider behavior:</p>

<h3 id="provider">PROVIDER</h3>

<p>This environment variable enforces a specific provider, bypassing the provider selection UI. This is useful for:</p>
<ul>
  <li>Dedicated deployments where only one provider should be available</li>
  <li>Automated environments and CI/CD pipelines</li>
  <li>Simplified user experience when provider choice is predetermined</li>
</ul>

<p>Accepted values:</p>
<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">None</code> - Enforces the Local Provider (no authentication)</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Meshery</code> - Enforces the Meshery (Meshery Cloud) Remote Provider</li>
  <li>Any other registered remote provider name</li>
</ul>

<p>Example: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER=None</code></p>

<p>When set, users are automatically directed to the specified provider’s login flow upon accessing Meshery.</p>

<h3 id="provider_capabilities_filepath">PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES_FILEPATH</h3>

<p>This environment variable allows you to specify a local file path to load provider capabilities from a static JSON file instead of fetching them from the remote provider’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/capabilities</code> endpoint. This is useful for:</p>
<ul>
  <li>Offline development and testing</li>
  <li>Environments with restricted network access</li>
  <li>Ensuring consistent provider capabilities across deployments</li>
</ul>

<p>Example: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES_FILEPATH=/path/to/capabilities.json</code></p>

<h3 id="skip_download_extensions">SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS</h3>

<p>This boolean environment variable controls whether Meshery downloads and refreshes provider extension packages. When set to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">true</code>, Meshery will skip downloading extension packages even when new versions are available. This is particularly useful for:</p>
<ul>
  <li>Development environments where you want to use locally modified extensions</li>
  <li>Deployments where extensions are pre-packaged or managed separately</li>
  <li>Reducing startup time and network bandwidth usage</li>
  <li>Preventing automatic updates to extension packages</li>
</ul>

<p>Default: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code> (extensions are downloaded/refreshed)</p>

<p>Example: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS=true</code></p>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> Extension downloads occur during:</p>
<ul>
  <li>User login (via the TokenHandler)</li>
  <li>Provider capability refresh operations</li>
  <li>Release channel updates</li>
</ul>

<p>When <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS</code> is enabled, existing extension packages will still be loaded if present, but no new versions will be retrieved.</p>

<h2 id="design-principles-meshery-remote-provider-framework">Design Principles: Meshery Remote Provider Framework</h2>

<p>Meshery’s Remote Provider extensibility framework is designed to enable the following functionalities:</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Pluggable UI Functionality</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Out-of-tree custom UI components with seamless user experience.</li>
      <li>A system of remote retrieval of extension packages (ReactJS components and Golang binaries).</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Pluggable Backend Functionality</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Remote Providers have any number of capabilities unbeknownst to Meshery.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Pluggable AuthZ</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Design an extensible role based access control system such that Remote Providers can determine their own set of controls. Remote Providers to return JWTs with custom roles, permission keys and permission keychains.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<h2 id="building-a-provider">Building a Provider</h2>

<p>Meshery interfaces with providers through a Go interface. The Provider implementations have to be placed in the code and compiled together today. A Provider instance will have to be injected into Meshery when the program starts.</p>

<p>Meshery keeps the implementation of Remote Providers separate so that they are brought in through a separate process and injected into Meshery at runtime (OR) change the way the code works to make the Providers invoke Meshery.</p>

<h3 id="verifying-compatibility-with-golang-version-update">Verifying Compatibility With Golang Version Update</h3>

<p>When Meshery is updated to a newer version of Golang, extension providers need to ensure their integrations remain compatible with the updated version. Changes in the Golang version can lead to compatibility issues, so it’s important to update your extension to align with Meshery’s new environment. For a detailed guide on how to verify and address any compatibility issues, refer to this <a href="./verify-compatibility">guide on verifying compatibility</a>.</p>

<h3 id="remote-provider-extension-points">Remote Provider Extension Points</h3>

<p>Interwoven into Meshery’s web-based user interface are a variety of extension points. Each extension point is carefully carved out to afford a seamless user experience. Each extension point is identified by a name and type. The following Meshery UI extension points are available:</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th><strong>Name</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Type</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Description</strong></th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>navigator</td>
      <td>Menu Items</td>
      <td>This is supposed to be a full page extension which will get a dedicated endpoint in the meshery UI. And will be listed in the meshery UI’s navigator/sidebar. Menu items may refer to full page extensions.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>user_prefs</td>
      <td>Single Component</td>
      <td>This is supposed to be remote react components which will get placed in a pre-existing page and will not have a dedicated endpoint. As of now, the only place where this extension can be loaded is the “User Preference” section under meshery settings.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>account</td>
      <td>Full Page</td>
      <td>Remote Reactjs components (or other) are placed in a pre-existing page and will have dedicated endpoint: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/extension/account</code>.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>collaborator</td>
      <td>Single Component</td>
      <td>This is supposed to be remote react components which will get placed in a pre-existing page and will not have a dedicated endpoint. Currently, placed at the Header component of Mehery UI. Its work is to show active Meshery users under the same remote provider.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>/extension/&lt;your name here&gt;</td>
      <td>Full Page</td>
      <td>The Provider package is unzipped into Meshery server filesystem under <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/app/provider-pkg/&lt;package-name&gt;</code>.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p>Remote Providers must fulfill the following endpoints:</p>

<ol>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/login</code> - return valid token</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/logout</code> - invalidating token</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/capabilities</code> - return capabilities.json</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="ui-extension-points">UI Extension Points</h2>

<p>All UI extensions will be hosted under the endpoint <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;mesheryserver:port/provider&gt;</code>.</p>

<h3 id="userprefs">UserPrefs</h3>

<p>The UserPrefs extension point expects and loads a component to be displayed into <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/userpreferences</code> page.</p>

<h3 id="navigator">Navigator</h3>

<p>The Navigator extension point loads a set of menu items to be displayed in the menu bar on the left hand side of the Meshery UI.</p>

<h2 id="provider-defined-redirects">Provider-Defined Redirects</h2>

<p>Remote Providers can define custom URL redirects through the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">redirects</code> field in the capabilities response. This allows providers to dynamically control how certain URL paths are handled by the Meshery server, enabling seamless navigation experiences for users.</p>

<h3 id="how-redirects-work">How Redirects Work</h3>

<p>When Meshery server receives a request for a specific URL path, it checks if the connected Remote Provider has defined a redirect for that path in its capabilities. If a matching redirect is found, the server issues an HTTP permanent redirect (308) to the target URL.</p>

<h3 id="configuring-redirects">Configuring Redirects</h3>

<p>Redirects are defined as a key-value map in the provider’s capabilities response, where:</p>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Key</strong>: The source URL path to intercept (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/</code>)</li>
  <li><strong>Value</strong>: The destination URL to redirect to (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/extension/meshmap</code>)</li>
</ul>

<p>Example configuration in the capabilities response:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">&quot;redirects&quot;: {
  &quot;/&quot;: &quot;/extension/meshmap&quot;,
  &quot;/dashboard&quot;: &quot;/extension/meshmap/dashboard&quot;
}</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="use-cases">Use Cases</h3>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Default Landing Page</strong>: Redirect users from the root path (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/</code>) to a custom extension page.</li>
  <li><strong>Custom Navigation</strong>: Guide users to specific extension pages based on their workflow.</li>
  <li><strong>URL Aliasing</strong>: Create shorter or more memorable URLs that redirect to extension endpoints.</li>
</ol>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Note</h4>
Redirects are evaluated before serving UI content. Only exact path matches are redirected.
</div>

<h2 id="capabilities-endpoint-example">Capabilities Endpoint Example</h2>

<p>Meshery Server will proxy all requests to remote provider endpoints. Endpoints are dynamically determined and identified in the <em><strong>capabilities</strong></em> section of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/capabilities</code> endpoint. Providers as an object have the following attributes (this must be returned as a response to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/capabilities</code> endpoint):</p>

<h4 id="meshery-server-registration">Meshery Server Registration</h4>

<p>Every Meshery server is capable of registering itself with the remote provider, considering that remote provider supports this feature as a capability.
On successful authentication with the remote provider, Meshery server registers itself by sending a POST request to the remote provider through the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">persist-connection</code> capability. The body of the request should include information so as to uniquely indentify Meshery server and its status.</p>

<p>Example of the request body:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">
  {
    &quot;server_id&quot;: &quot;xxxx-xxxxx-xxxx-xxxx&quot;,
    &quot;server_version&quot;: &quot;vx.x.x&quot;,
    &quot;server_build-sha&quot;: &quot;xxxx-xxxxx&quot;,
    &quot;server_location&quot;: &quot;&lt;protocol&gt;://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;”
  }
</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="configurable-oauth-callback-url">Configurable OAuth Callback URL</h2>

<p>As of the release <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">v0.5.39</code>, Meshery Server has extended its capability to configure the callback URL for connected <em>Remote Providers</em>. This is helpful when you are deploying Meshery behind an ingress gateway or reverse proxy. You can specify a custom, redirect endpoint for the connected Remote Provider.
Let’s understand this through an example deployment scenario below.</p>

<h3 id="example-deployment-scenario-meshery-cloud-istio-and-azure-kubernetes-service">Example Deployment Scenario: Meshery Cloud, Istio, and Azure Kubernetes Service</h3>

<p>User has deployed the Meshery behind a Istio Ingress Gateway and the Istio is also behind an Application Gateway (e.g. AKS Application Gateway). Generally, when you use a GitHub Remote Provider for authentication, it redirect the request to the Istio Ingress Gateway FQDN. In this setup, redirection won’t be successful because the Ingress Gateway is behind an additional Application Gateway. In this case, you have to define where the request should be redirected once it is authenticated from GitHub.</p>

<p><strong><em>SOLUTION</em></strong></p>

<p>You can define a custom callback URL by setting up the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> environment variable while installing Meshery.</p>

<p><strong>Example using Helm</strong></p>

<p>First, construct the URL in the format
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">https://[CUSTOM_URL]/api/user/token</code></p>

<ul>
  <li>Where <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">[CUSTOM_URL]</code> is the URL where <strong>Meshery server</strong> will be or is installed. For example, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">https://k8s-staging.test.io/</code>.</li>
  <li>And <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">api/user/token</code> is the <strong>Auth Endpoint</strong> and is append at the end of your custom URL.</li>
</ul>

<p>So, the final URL would look similar to
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">https://k8s-staging.test.io/api/user/token</code></p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Note</h4>
Callback URL is not the same as Provider URL. In scenarios where Meshery server and Provider is installed on same server, pay attention to paths or subdomains.
</div>

<p>Next, set the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> variable when running the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">helm install</code>. Below is an example:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">helm install meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery --set env.MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=&lt;https://k8s-staging.test.io/api/user/token&gt;
</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p><strong>NOTE</strong></p>

<p>If Meshery server is accessible in a path of the URL such as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">https://k8s-staging.test.io/meshery</code>, then the callback URL will be <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">https://k8s-staging.test.io/meshery/api/user/token</code>.</p>

<h2 id="managing-your-remote-provider-extension-code">Managing your Remote Provider Extension Code</h2>

<p>Remote Provider extensions are kept out-of-tree from Meshery (server and UI). You might need to build your extensions under the same environment and set of dependencies as Meshery. The Meshery framework of extensibility has been designed such that in-tree extensions can be safely avoided while still providing a robust platform from which to extend Meshery’s functionality. Often, herein lies the delineation of open vs. closed functionality within Meshery. Remote Providers can bring (plugin) what functionality that they want behind this extensible interface (more about Meshery extensibility), at least that is up to the point that Meshery has provided a way to plug that feature in.</p>

<p>Offering out-of-tree support for Meshery extensions means that:</p>

<ol>
  <li>source code to your Meshery extensions are not required to be open source,</li>
  <li>liability to Meshery’s stability is significantly reduced, avoiding potential bugs in extended components.</li>
</ol>

<p>Through clearly defined extension points, Meshery extensions may be offered as closed source capabilities that plug into open source Meshery code. To facilitate integration of your Meshery extensions, you might automate the building and releasing of your separate, but interdependent code repositories. You will be responsible for sustaining both your ReactJS and Golang-based extensions.</p>
   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Extensibility: UI</h1>
           <p>Meshery UI has a number of extension points that allow you to greatly customize both its functional behavior and visual appearance. These extension points come in different types, and this document describes each type, its example use, best practices to consider, and caveats of which to be aware.</p>

<h3 id="extensibility-customizing-text-based-forms-using-rjsf-custom-component">Extensibility: Customizing Text-based Forms using RJSF Custom Component</h3>

<p>RJSFWrapperComponent provides customizations for RJSF forms, overriding the default behavior of meshery-ui rjsf forms. The <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/0bc68d1cd0ba80a565afa68bce80899c22db9a2e/ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/RJSF.js#L66">Rjsf forms are wrapped</a> in this component to receive custom props from a Meshery extension.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">
&lt;RJSFWrapperComponent {...props}&gt;
  &lt;RJSFForm
    isLoading={isLoading}
    schema={schema}
    data={data}
    onChange={(e) =&gt; {
      setData(e.formData)
    }}
    jsonSchema={jsonSchema}
  /&gt;
&lt;/RJSFWrapperComponent&gt;
</code>
</div>
</pre>
<p>See this <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/0bc68d1cd0ba80a565afa68bce80899c22db9a2e/ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/RJSF.js#L91">RJSF Component</a> as an example of how these properties are received.</p>

<h3 id="extensibility-user-accounts">Extensibility: User Accounts</h3>

<p>Meshery Server uses <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">Providers</a> for identity management. Providers can implement the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">user_account</code> extension to handle custom user management scenarios. The user avatar behavior, which changes based on the user’s status, can be customized by extending the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/7de49ef4928f114080f923f2ad261f4433ca91d6/ui/components/User.js#L46">User Component</a>.</p>

<h3 id="build-time-ui-extensibility">Build-Time UI Extensibility</h3>

<p>Meshery offers powerful customization options for its web application user interface at build time. This feature allows developers to tailor the UI to specific needs by modifying component behavior, managing routes, and applying custom themes.</p>

<h5 id="configuration-file">Configuration File</h5>

<p>The build-time UI customization is controlled through the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ui.config.js</code> file. This file supports various configuration options to modify the Meshery UI.</p>

<h5 id="current-features">Current Features</h5>

<p><em>Component Management</em></p>

<p>You can control the visibility and behavior of various UI components. For example:</p>

<div class="language-javascript highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nx">module</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">exports</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="na">components</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="na">navigator</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="c1">// Set to false to disable the navigator component (default: true)</span>
    <span class="c1">// Add other components here as needed</span>
  <span class="p">},</span>
<span class="p">};</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p><em>Upcoming Features</em></p>

<p>Meshery is continuously expanding its UI extensibility capabilities. The following features are planned for future releases:</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Route Management</strong>: Ability to disable or modify specific routes.</li>
  <li><strong>Redirect Configuration</strong>: Set up custom redirects within the application.</li>
  <li><strong>Custom Theming</strong>: Apply custom themes to personalize the look and feel of the Meshery UI.</li>
</ol>

<h4 id="usage">Usage</h4>

<p>To customize the Meshery UI:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Locate the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ui.config.js</code> file in your Meshery project.</li>
  <li>Modify the configuration options according to your requirements.</li>
  <li>Rebuild the Meshery application to apply your changes.</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="loading-screen-message-persistence">Loading Screen Message Persistence</h3>

<p>Meshery UI displays a randomly selected loading message while the application and extensions load. To ensure a consistent user experience, the same loading message is displayed across all loading screens (main UI and extensions) during a single session.</p>

<h4 id="how-it-works">How It Works</h4>

<p>The loading message is selected once and stored in the browser’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">window</code> object (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">window.__mesheryLoadingMessage</code>). All subsequent loading screens retrieve this persisted message, preventing jarring re-renders with different messages.</p>

<h4 id="using-the-persisted-loading-message-in-ui-plugins">Using the Persisted Loading Message in UI Plugins</h4>

<p><strong>No changes needed</strong> for plugins that:</p>
<ul>
  <li>Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DynamicFullScreenLoader</code> (already imports <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">randomLoadingMessage</code>)</li>
  <li>Are loaded through the main Meshery UI framework</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>For standalone loaders</strong>, import the persisted message:</p>

<div class="language-javascript highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">randomLoadingMessage</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">@/components/LoadingComponents/loadingMessages</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="c1">// or</span>
<span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">getPersistedLoadingMessage</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">@/components/LoadingComponents/loadingMessages</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="c1">// Then use in your loading component:</span>
<span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">LoadingScreen</span> <span class="nx">message</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">randomLoadingMessage</span><span class="p">}</span> <span class="sr">/</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span></code></pre></div></div>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">randomLoadingMessage</code> export automatically retrieves the persisted value from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">window.__mesheryLoadingMessage</code>, ensuring consistency across all loaders in your plugin.</p>

<h4 id="passing-new-custom-prop-to-forms">Passing new custom prop to forms:</h4>

<ol>
  <li>Pass the new prop from the Meshery Extension in the RJSF Wrapper component used like this:</li>
</ol>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs"> function RJSFWrapperComponent(props) {
// Clone the child to pass in additional props
const children = React.cloneElement(props.children, {
...(props.children?.props || {}),
customComponent: YOUR_NEW_CUSTOM_COMPONENT_OR_PROP
});

return children
}</code>
</div>
</pre>
<p>Extract the props in the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/0bc68d1cd0ba80a565afa68bce80899c22db9a2e/ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/RJSF.js#L91">RJSFForm Component</a></p>

<p><em>Extensibility documentation missing?</em>
Submit an issue to request more documentation.</p>

<h3 id="extension-points-by-file">Extension Points by File</h3>

<ol>
  <li><strong>/ui/components/NavigatorExtension.js</strong> - add custom menu items in Meshery’s main navigation menu.</li>
  <li><strong>/ui/pages/extension/[component].js</strong> - optionally, define the state of a parent menu item: expanded or collapsed.</li>
  <li><strong>ui/remote-component.config.js</strong> - list of Material UI components made available to Remote Providers and their plugins.</li>
  <li><strong>ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternServiceFormCore.js</strong> - PatternServiceFormCore component which decouples the SettingsForm and TraitsForm from their UI representation while keeping the logic coupled. This design lets the Remote Provider amend the design of the components without interfering with Meshery UI’s core logic.</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="using-react-json-schema-form">Using React JSON Schema Form</h3>

<p>Meshery exposes a custom RJSF Form component which is capable of generating “Pattern” YAMLs without being extremely opinionated about the UI. This custom component is available at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternServiceFormCore.js</code>. An example usage of the component which will render the logically coupled <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SettingsForm</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">TraitsForm</code> in a Material UI <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">TabPanel</code>:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs"> &lt;PatternServiceFormCore
formData={formData}
schemaSet={schemaSet}
onSubmit={onSubmit}
onDelete={onDelete}
reference={reference}
namespace={namespace}

&gt;

    {(SettingsForm, TraitsForm) =&gt; {
    	return (
    		&lt;div&gt;
    			&lt;TabPanel value={tab} index={0} style={ { marginTop: &quot;1.1rem&quot; } }&gt;
    				&lt;SettingsForm /&gt;
    			&lt;/TabPanel&gt;
    			&lt;TabPanel value={tab} index={1} style={ { marginTop: &quot;1.1rem&quot; } }&gt;
    				&lt;TraitsForm /&gt;
    			&lt;/TabPanel&gt;
    		&lt;/div&gt;
    	);
    }}

&lt;/PatternServiceFormCore&gt;</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Meshery UI’s RJSF form accepts two props:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">RJSFWrapperComponent</code>: The wrapper component gets all of the props that are passed to the underlying form, allowing to inspect the props and changing the behaviour based on them.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">RJSFFormChildComponent</code>: This component will customize the internals of the RJSF form.</li>
</ul>

<p>With both of these props, Remote Providers can customize the wrapper and can also customize the body of the form. This allows full customization of the form.</p>

<p>from <em>ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/index.js</em></p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">function PatternService({ formData, jsonSchema, onChange, type, onSubmit, onDelete, RJSFWrapperComponent, RJSFFormChildComponent })</code>
</div>
</pre>
   <br/>


        </div>
      </main>

        <div class="content-table">
          <div class="content-table__editable">

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Ensuring Extension Compatibility with Meshery</h1>
           <p>The Meshery ecosystem is designed for extensibility, with the core platform (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery/meshery</code>) providing extension points for a variety of plugins, collectively managed in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery-extensions</code> GitHub organization. To ensure a stable and seamless user experience, it is critical that extensions remain compatible with the Meshery platform, especially when shared frameworks or dependencies are updated.</p>

<p>This guide outlines the key areas of compatibility and provides a general process for extension developers to follow when Meshery’s underlying frameworks are updated.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Meshery's Bill of Materials</h4>
Meshery's version is defined by its <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing#meshery-contribution-flow">Bill of Materials (BOM)</a>, which specifies versions for Go, Node.js, and other key dependencies. Extension developers should reference the BOM to ensure alignment.
</div>

<h2 id="key-areas-for-compatibility">Key Areas for Compatibility</h2>

<p>Compatibility between Meshery and its extensions spans several areas. When the Meshery platform is updated, one or more of the following are likely to change:</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Language Runtimes</strong>: Meshery and its extensions are often built using the same programming languages. Ensuring version alignment is the first step to compatibility.
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Go Version</strong>: Meshery is primarily written in Go. Extensions written in Go must be compiled with the same major Go version to ensure binary compatibility.</li>
      <li><strong>Node.js Version</strong>: UI extensions may depend on the Node.js version used by Meshery’s UI.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Shared Go Libraries</strong>: Meshery and its extensions share a common set of libraries (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery/meshkit</code>) that provide foundational utilities, API clients, and data models.
    <ul>
      <li><strong>MeshKit</strong>: Extensions must depend on the same version of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshkit</code> as the Meshery server to avoid mismatches in data structures and function signatures.</li>
      <li><strong>gRPC and Protobuf</strong>: Meshery uses gRPC for communication. Extensions must use the same Protobuf definitions (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.proto</code> files) and generated Go code to ensure API compatibility.</li>
      <li><strong>Other Dependencies</strong>: Align versions of other critical shared dependencies listed in Meshery’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">go.mod</code>.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>UI Frameworks and Component Libraries</strong>: UI-based extensions must align with Meshery’s frontend technology stack to ensure a consistent user experience and functional correctness.
    <ul>
      <li><strong>React and Next.js</strong>: Align with the versions used in Meshery’s UI.</li>
      <li><strong>Material-UI (MUI)</strong>: Use the same version of the MUI component library to maintain visual consistency.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Build and CI/CD Tooling</strong>: The build process for extensions should be compatible with the environment and tooling used by Meshery.
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Makefiles</strong>: Variables and targets in the core Meshery Makefiles (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">install/Makefile.core.mk</code>) may be updated.</li>
      <li><strong>Docker Images</strong>: Base Docker images used for building and running Meshery may be updated, affecting the extension’s build environment.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<h2 id="general-process-for-verifying-compatibility">General Process for Verifying Compatibility</h2>

<p>When Meshery’s Bill of Materials is updated, follow this general process to verify and update your extension.</p>

<h3 id="1-identify-the-changes-in-meshery">1. Identify the Changes in Meshery</h3>

<p>Start by reviewing the release notes or commit history of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery/meshery</code> repository to understand what has changed. Pay close attention to:</p>
<ul>
  <li>Go version updates in the root <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">go.mod</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">install/Makefile.core.mk</code>.</li>
  <li>Version changes for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery/meshkit</code> and other key dependencies in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">go.mod</code>.</li>
  <li>Updates to UI framework versions in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ui/package.json</code>.</li>
  <li>Changes to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.proto</code> files for gRPC services.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="2-update-your-extensions-dependencies">2. Update Your Extension’s Dependencies</h3>

<p>In your extension’s repository, update your dependency files to match the versions used in Meshery.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>For Go-based extensions</strong>:
    <ol>
      <li>Update the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">go</code> directive in your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">go.mod</code> file to match Meshery’s.</li>
      <li>Update the required version of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">github.com/meshery/meshkit</code> and other shared modules:
        <div class="language-sh highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>go get github.com/meshery/meshkit@vX.X.X
go mod tidy
</code></pre></div>        </div>
      </li>
    </ol>
  </li>
  <li><strong>For UI-based extensions</strong>:
    <ol>
      <li>Update the versions of React, Next.js, MUI, and other relevant packages in your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">package.json</code>.</li>
      <li>Run <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">npm install</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">yarn install</code> to update your dependencies.</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
</ul>

<h3 id="3-rebuild-and-test-your-extension">3. Rebuild and Test Your Extension</h3>

<p>After updating the dependencies, rebuild your extension to ensure it compiles without errors.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>For Go-based extensions</strong>:
    <div class="language-sh highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  go build <span class="nt">-o</span> &lt;your-extension-binary&gt;
</code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
  <li><strong>For UI-based extensions</strong>:
    <div class="language-sh highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  npm run build
</code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
</ul>

<h3 id="4-perform-integration-testing">4. Perform Integration Testing</h3>

<p>Run your updated extension with the latest version of Meshery to verify end-to-end compatibility.</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Run the latest Meshery server</strong>. Ensure you are using the build corresponding to the dependency updates.</li>
  <li><strong>Run your updated extension</strong>.</li>
  <li><strong>Monitor the logs</strong> of both Meshery and your extension for any runtime errors, panics, or warnings related to version mismatches.</li>
  <li><strong>Thoroughly test your extension’s functionality</strong>. Verify that all interactions with Meshery are working as expected, including API calls and UI integrations.</li>
</ol>

<p>By following this process, you can ensure that your extension remains compatible with the ever-evolving Meshery platform, providing a reliable and consistent experience for all users.</p>
   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>
