        <div class="td-content">
           <h1 id="import-and-export-designs">Import and Export Designs</h1>

<p>Meshery supports two primary operations for working with designs: <strong>Import</strong> and <strong>Export</strong>.
A <strong><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/designs">design</a></strong> in Meshery is a structured model describing how various components (e.g., Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, or Docker Compose objects) should be managed and deployed. This document details the core concepts, the import/export processes, and the available methods to perform them.</p>

<h2 id="core-operations">Core Operations</h2>

<p>Meshery treats each design as a combination of:</p>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Components</strong>: Defined resources or services (e.g., Deployments, Services).</li>
  <li><strong>Relationships</strong>: Possible connections or dependencies among components (e.g., hierarchical, sibling, edge).</li>
</ul>

<p>When <strong>importing</strong> a design, Meshery:</p>
<ol>
  <li><strong>Parses</strong> and <strong>validates</strong> the design file.</li>
  <li>Processes design structure, applying transformations as needed.</li>
  <li><strong>Routes</strong> validated components to the appropriate Meshery Adapters for further deployment or processing.</li>
</ol>

<p>When <strong>exporting</strong> a design, Meshery:</p>
<ol>
  <li><strong>Fetches</strong> the design data from the Meshery database using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/api/pattern/download/{id}</code>.</li>
  <li><strong>Converts</strong> the design format if necessary (e.g., from V1alpha2 to V1beta1).</li>
  <li><strong>Applies</strong> requested export format (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">current</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">original</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">oci</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">helm-chart</code>).</li>
  <li><strong>Sends</strong> the exported design file for download as a YAML file or OCI artifact or Helm chart(.tgz).</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="import-methods">Import Methods</h2>

<p>You can import designs into Meshery through either <strong><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/reference/mesheryctl">Meshery CLI</a></strong> or <strong>Meshery UI</strong>.</p>

<h4 id="1-using-meshery-cli">1. Using Meshery CLI</h4>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl design import <span class="nt">--file</span> &lt;PATH/URL&gt; <span class="nt">--source-type</span> &lt;TYPE&gt;
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c"># Example: Import Kubernetes manifest</span>
mesheryctl design import <span class="nt">-f</span> ./app-deployment.yaml <span class="nt">-s</span> manifest
</code></pre></div></div>

<h4 id="2-using-meshery-ui">2. Using Meshery UI</h4>

<ol>
  <li>Go to <strong>Designs &gt; Import Design</strong>.</li>
  <li>Choose your input method.</li>
  <li>Select the source type from the dropdown (e.g., Kubernetes manifest, Helm chart).</li>
  <li>Submit the design for processing.</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="import-processing-details">Import Processing Details</h3>

<p>After you initiate an import, Meshery executes a <strong>dataflow sequence</strong> to properly handle the design:</p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Client submits a design</strong>
A POST request is sent to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/api/pattern/import</code>, containing a design file. If the design is sourced from Kubernetes Manifests, Docker Compose, or Helm Charts, it is first converted into a standard Kubernetes Manifest.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Pattern Engine queries registry</strong>
Meshery queries the component registry to match the design’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kind</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">apiVersion</code>, and other identifiers. If the design originates from non-Meshery formats, Meshery attempts to transform it accordingly.</p>
  </li>
  <li><strong>System converts design format</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Converts Helm Charts, Docker Compose, and Kubernetes Manifests into Meshery Design.</li>
      <li>Removes unnecessary fields and ensures compatibility.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Validated components are stored in Meshery</strong>
Once validated, the design is stored in Meshery. Users can later deploy it to a supported platform (e.g., Kubernetes, Consul, Istio) using Meshery UI or CLI.</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="export-methods">Export Methods</h2>

<p>Designs can also be exported either via <strong>Meshery CLI</strong> or <strong>Meshery UI</strong>. During export, Meshery gathers the design’s components, relationships, and metadata into a specified format.</p>

<h4 id="1-using-meshery-cli-1">1. Using Meshery CLI</h4>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl design <span class="nb">export</span> <span class="nt">--type</span> &lt;FORMAT&gt; <span class="nt">--output</span> &lt;DIRECTORY&gt;
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c"># Example: Export to OCI format</span>
mesheryctl design <span class="nb">export</span> <span class="nt">--type</span> oci <span class="nt">-o</span> ./exports
</code></pre></div></div>

<h4 id="2-using-meshery-ui-1">2. Using Meshery UI</h4>

<ol>
  <li>Go to <strong>Designs &gt; My Designs</strong> and select the design you want to export.</li>
  <li>Click the <strong>Export</strong> action button.</li>
  <li>Choose an export format (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">current</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">original</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">oci</code>).</li>
  <li>Specify the download location for your exported file.</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="summary">Summary</h2>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Import</strong>: Meshery parses and validates your design, converts non-Meshery formats (e.g., Kubernetes Manifests, Helm Charts, Docker Compose) into Meshery Designs, and stores the design in Meshery. Users can later deploy it to the correct adapters as needed.</li>
  <li><strong>Export</strong>: Meshery <strong>retrieves</strong> the design from storage, <strong>converts</strong> its format if needed, <strong>packages</strong> it in the selected format (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">current</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">original</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">oci</code>), and <strong>delivers</strong> it as a YAML file or OCI artifact via CLI or UI download.</li>
</ul>

  src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Extensions</h1>
           <p>Extensions in Meshery are additional plugins or add-ons that provide extra functionalities beyond the core features of the platform. These extensions can be used to customize, extend and integrate with other tools and services.</p>

<ul>
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensions/import-export-designs">Import and Export Designs</a>
      
        -  Manage and transfer Meshery designs seamlessly through import and export using CLI and UI.
      
      </li>
      
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensions/-snapshot"> Snapshot</a>
      
        -  Screenshot service provided via  to capture a snapshot of your infrastructure at any given time.
      
      </li>
      
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensions">Extensions</a>
      
        -  Extensions are additional plugins or add-ons that provide extra functionalities beyond the core features of the Meshery.
      
      </li>
      
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensions/"></a>
      
        -  Collaborative cloud native visual designer to design and manage infrastructure and applications.
      
      </li>
      
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensions/helm--snapshot">Helm  Snapshot</a>
      
        -  Helm CLI plugin to visually render a snapshot of your Helm charts.
      
      </li>
      
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensions/kubectl-meshsync-snapshot">kubectl MeshSync Snapshot</a>
      
        -  A native kubectl plugin for conveniently synchronizing the state of your cluster with Meshery Server.
      
      </li>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Meshery Integrations</h1>
           <p>Meshery provides 220+ built-in integrations which refer to the supported connections and interactions between Meshery and various cloud native platforms, tools, and technologies. Meshery’s approach is Kubernetes-native which means you can easily incorporate Meshery into your existing workflow without additional setup or integration effort.</p>

<h3 id="all-integrations-by-name-391">All Integrations by Name (391)</h3>

<p>Optionally, you can <a href="https://meshery.io/integrations">navigate all integrations visually</a>.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
           <h1 id="-kubectl-meshsync-snapshot"><img style="height: 4rem; width: 4rem;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/meshsync/meshsync.svg" /> kubectl MeshSync Snapshot</h1>

<p>A <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kubectl</code> plugin for performing an ad hoc collection of resource information from a Kubernetes cluster and sending the cluster resources details to a Meshery Server. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kubectl meshsync snapshot</code> is a native kubectl plugin for conveniently synchronizing the state of your cluster with Meshery Server.</p>

<hr />

<h2 id="about-meshery-extensions">About Meshery Extensions</h2>

<p><a href="https://meshery.io/extensions">Meshery Extensions</a> are plugins or add-ons that enhance the functionality of the Meshery platform beyond its core capabilities. Meshery supports different types of extensions (<a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensions/">docs</a>):</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/architecture/adapters">Adapters</a>: Adapters allow Meshery to interface with the different cloud native infrastructure.</li>
  <li><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensibility/load-generators">Load Generators</a>: for performance characterization and benchmarking</li>
  <li><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensibility/integrations">Integrations</a>: model-based support for a broad variety of design and orchestration of cloud and cloud native platforms, tools, and technologies.</li>
  <li><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensibility/providers">Providers</a>: for connecting to different cloud providers and infrastructure platforms</li>
  <li><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensibility/ui">UI Plugins</a>: Meshery UI has a number of extension points that allow users to customize their experience with third-party plugins.</li>
</ul>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Creating a Meshery Design</h1>
           <div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Learn about Designs</h4>
Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">what a Meshery Design</a> is and how it fits into Meshery's approach to cloud native management.
</div>

<h2 id="ways-to-create-a-meshery-design">Ways to create a Meshery Design</h2>

<p>You can create a Meshery design in two ways:</p>

<h3 id="from-scratch">From scratch</h3>

<ol>
  <li>Click on the “Design” tab to start creating a new design.</li>
  <li>In the left panel, click “Components” and browse the type of component you want to add.</li>
  <li>Drag and drop the components onto the canvas.</li>
  <li>Click and drag from one component to another to create connections between components. You can customize the connections by adding labels or adjusting their properties.</li>
  <li>Once you’re satisfied with your design, click the “Save” button on the toolbar. Your design will be saved as “Untitled design” by default. You can give your design a name to help identify and manage it later.</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="from-a-template">From a template</h3>

<p>Another way to create a Meshery design is to use an already curated template. You can either import designs that others have published and made available for public use or clone patterns from the Meshery Catalog.</p>

<h4 id="importing-published-designs">Importing published designs</h4>

<ol>
  <li>In the left panel of the designer mode, click “Designs”.</li>
  <li>Select a design from the list that appears in the panel and it will appear on your canvas.</li>
  <li>If you already have a design that you’d like to build on, click on the import icon to import the design directly to your  canvas.</li>
  <li>A modal will pop-up where you’ll then select the design type, choose the upload method (file upload or url import), enter the design file name, and choose the file to upload or enter the url link to import.</li>
</ol>

<h4 id="cloning-patterns-from-catalog">Cloning patterns from Catalog</h4>

<ol>
  <li>In the left panel of the designer mode, click “Catalog”.</li>
  <li>Select a design from the list that appears in the panel.</li>
  <li>A modal will pop up requesting you to clone (create a copy of) the design you’ve selected.</li>
  <li>Click “clone” and a copy of the design will appear on your  canvas. You can then configure the design to suit your purposes.</li>
</ol>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Learn about Patterns</h4>
Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/patterns">what a Meshery Pattern</a> is and how it fits into Meshery's approach to cloud native management.
</div>

   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Create Models</h1>
           <p>Meshery offers two primary ways to bring models into your system: <strong>Create</strong> and <strong><a href="/v0.8/guides/configuration-management/importing-models">Import</a></strong>.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Import</strong> is ideal when you already have a model definition file (e.g., JSON, CSV) and simply want to bring it into Meshery.</li>
  <li><strong>Create</strong> is the recommended approach if you’re starting fresh — it guides you through building a model step by step using an intuitive UI wizard.</li>
</ul>

<p>This section walks you through the <strong>Create</strong> workflow — perfect for users who want full control over naming, styling, and categorizing their models while sourcing CRDs from GitHub or ArtifactHub.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Tip: If you don’t have any files yet, start with <strong>Create</strong>. You can always <a href="/v0.8/guides/configuration-management/exporting-models">export</a> or re-import your model later.</p>
</blockquote>

<div class="tab-container">

  <!-- First Level Tab: Meshery UI -->
  <input type="radio" id="tab1" name="tabs" checked="" />
  <label for="tab1">
    <i class="fa fa-desktop"></i> Meshery UI
  </label>
  <section class="tabbed">
    <p>The URL Create feature allows you to create models in Meshery by providing URLs to source repositories or package registries. Here's how to use it:</p>

    <h4>Step 1: Open the Model Generation Interface</h4>
    <p>Go to the <a href="https://playground.meshery.io/settings?settingsCategory=Registry&amp;tab=Models">Registry</a> section in the Meshery UI. Click the <strong>create</strong> button to start creating a new model.</p>

    <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-where.gif">
      <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-where.gif" alt="registry generate model" style="width: 50%; max-width: 400px;" />
    </a>

    <h4>Step 2: Set Up Your Model Name</h4>
    <p>Enter the following names for your model:</p>
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Model Name:</strong> This is the unique, system identifier. Use lowercase letters and hyphens only (no spaces). <br />Example: <code>cert-manager</code></li>
      <li><strong>Display Name:</strong> This is the friendly name displayed in the UI. It can include spaces and uppercase letters. <br />Example: <code>Cert Manager</code></li>
    </ul>

    <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-name.png">
      <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-name.png" alt="registry generate model name" style="width: 50%; max-width: 400px;" />
    </a>

    <h4>Step 3: Set Model Categorization</h4>
    <p>Select the appropriate <strong>Category</strong> and <strong>Subcategory</strong> from the dropdowns. If your model doesn't match any available category, choose Uncategorized to ensure it can be easily located later.</p>

    <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-category.png">
      <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-category.png" alt="registry generate model categorization" style="width: 50%; max-width: 400px;" />
    </a>

    <h4>Step 4: Configure Model Styling</h4>
    <p>Customize your model's appearance:</p>
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Logos:</strong> Upload separate images for dark and light themes.</li>
      <li><strong>Colors:</strong> Define the primary and secondary colors for your model's visual elements.</li>
      <li><strong>Icon Shape:</strong> Choose a shape for the model’s icon as displayed in the UI.</li>
    </ul>
    <p>Note: If you don't provide custom styling, Meshery's default values will be used.</p>

    <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-styling.png">
      <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-styling.png" alt="registry generate model styling" style="width: 50%; max-width: 400px;" />
    </a>

    <h4>Step 5: Provide the Source Location</h4>
    <p>Specify the source for your model by entering one of the following URL types:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>
        <strong>GitHub Repository:</strong><br />
        Enter a URL using the following format:  
        <code>git://github.com/[organization]/[repository]/[branch]/path/to/crds</code><br />
        Example:  
        <code>git://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/master/deploy/crds</code>
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>ArtifactHub Package:</strong><br />
        Enter a URL in this format:  
        <code>https://artifacthub.io/packages/search?ts_query_web={model-name}</code>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <div class="alert alert-light">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Need a Source URL?</h4>
Check the <code>sourceURL</code> column in the <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1DZHnzxYWOlJ69Oguz4LkRVTFM79kC2tuvdwizOJmeMw" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Meshery Integration Sheet</a> and try one of the listed sources.
</div>


    <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-source.png">
      <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-source.png" alt="registry generate model source selection" style="width: 50%; max-width: 400px;" />
    </a>

    <h4>Step 6: Additional Settings</h4>
    <ul>
    <li><strong>Immediate Registration:</strong> Enable this option to register your model instantly, making it available in your Meshery instance right away.</li>
    <li><strong>Visual Annotation Only:</strong> Mark this option if your model is intended solely for visual diagramming rather than infrastructure management.</li>
    </ul>

    <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-details.png">
      <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-details.png" alt="registry generate model additional settings" style="width: 50%; max-width: 400px;" />
    </a>

     <div class="alert alert-light">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Visual Annotation Models</h4>
When a model is marked for visual annotation only, it means the model will be used purely for visualization and diagramming purposes within Meshery's interface, rather than for actual infrastructure management.
</div>


    <h4>Step 7: Finalize and Create Your Model</h4>
    <p>Review your model details. If everything looks good, click "Generate" to create your model.</p>
    <p>Meshery will process the provided source URL, extract the necessary information, and create the model based on the specified details.</p>
    <p>If you want to make any changes before generation, you can go back to the previous steps using the navigation buttons and edit the details as needed.</p>

    <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-finalize.png">
      <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/registry/create-ui-finalize.png" alt="registry generate model generate" style="width: 50%; max-width: 400px;" />
    </a>

    <h4>Step 8: Check Model Generation Status</h4>
    <p>Once the model is successfully generated, a confirmation message will appear. You'll be able to view the model along with its components and relationships directly in the Registry page.</p>
    <p>If any issues occur, Meshery will display an error message detailing what went wrong so you can correct it and try again.</p>
    <p>A notification will also appear in the <a href="/v0.8/guides/events-management">Notification Center</a> to confirm whether the operation succeeded or failed, providing additional context if needed.</p>

    <div class="alert alert-warning">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Note on Deletion</h4>
Once a model is generated, it cannot be deleted from the Meshery UI. If you no longer wish to use it, you may mark it as ignored instead.
</div>

    
    </section>

  <!-- Second Level Tab: mesheryctl -->
  <input type="radio" id="tab2" name="tabs" />
  <label for="tab2">
    <i class="fa fa-terminal"></i> mesheryctl
  </label>
  <section class="tabbed">
    <h3>Prerequisites:</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>Fork the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery" target="_blank" rel="noopener">meshery/meshery repository.</a></li>
      <li>Install the Meshery CLI by following the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/installation/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">installation instructions.</a></li>
    </ul>

    <div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Generating Models does not require Meshery Server</h4>
Meshery Server is not required to generate models. The Meshery CLI can be used to generate models. Model and Component generation logic is MeshKit. `mesheryctl` and Meshery Server both utilize MeshKit’s libraries for ongoing programmatic generation of models and components.
</div>


    <br />
    <!-- Second Level Tabs under mesheryctl -->
    <div class="tab-container">
      <!-- CSV Method -->
      <input type="radio" id="csv-tab" name="mesheryctl-tabs" checked="" />
      <label for="csv-tab">
        <i class="fa fa-list"></i> Using CSV
      </label>
      <section class="tabbed">
        <h4>1. Understanding the Template Directory</h4>
        <p>Inside your forked Meshery repository, you'll find the templates-csvs directory containing three essential CSV files:</p>
        <code>
            mesheryctl/templates/templates-csvs/
                <br />
                ├── models.csv       # Define model metadata and core properties
                <br />
                ├── components.csv   # Specify individual components and their characteristics
                <br />
                └── relationships.csv # Define how components interact and connect
                <br />
        </code>

        <h4>2. Customizing Your Model</h4>
        <p>Creating your model involves modifying these CSV files to match your specific requirements. When making changes, you have two valuable references at your disposal: the existing entries in the CSV files serve as practical examples, while the <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1DZHnzxYWOlJ69Oguz4LkRVTFM79kC2tuvdwizOJmeMw">integration spreadsheet</a> provides comprehensive documentation of all possible fields and their purposes.</p>

        <h4>3. Generating Your Model</h4>
        <p>Once you've customized your CSV files, you can generate your model using a single command. Ensure you're in the root directory of your forked Meshery repository, as this maintains the correct file path relationships:</p>
        <code>mesheryctl registry generate --directory templates-csvs --model "YOUR_MODEL_NAME"</code>

        <h4>4. Locating Generated Files</h4>
        <p>After successful generation, your model's files will be created in the Meshery server's model directory. You can find these files at <code>meshery/server/meshmodel/[YOUR_MODEL_NAME]/</code>. Take time to review these generated files to ensure they accurately reflect your intended model structure.</p>

        <h4>5. Troubleshooting</h4>
        <p>If you encounter issues during the generation process, you can use these diagnostic approaches to identify and resolve problems:</p>
        <ul>
          <li>Examine the detailed error logs at <code>~/.meshery/logs/registry/</code> to understand specific generation issues.</li>
          <li>Review your CSV files for proper formatting, ensuring all required columns are present and correctly populated.</li>
          <li>Confirm you're executing the command from the root of your forked Meshery repository.</li>
        </ul>
      </section>

      <!-- Spreadsheet Method -->
      <input type="radio" id="spreadsheet-tab" name="mesheryctl-tabs" />
      <label for="spreadsheet-tab">
        <i class="fa fa-table"></i> Using Integration Spreadsheet
      </label>
      <section class="tabbed">
        <h3>Setting Up Your Environment</h3>
        <p>Before you begin working with the Integration Spreadsheet, you'll need to complete several important setup steps:</p>

        <h4>1. Spreadsheet Preparation</h4>
        <p>Start by creating your own copy of the Meshery Integration Sheet:</p>
        <ol>
          <li>Visit the <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1DZHnzxYWOlJ69Oguz4LkRVTFM79kC2tuvdwizOJmeMw" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Meshery Integration Sheet</a></li>
          <li>Make a copy using File &gt; Make a copy</li>
          <li>Look at the URL of your new spreadsheet and note the ID (the long string between /d/ and /edit)</li>
        </ol>

        <h4>2. Google Cloud Configuration</h4>
        <p>Set up your Google Cloud environment with these steps:</p>
        <ol>
          <li><a href="https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-project" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Create a new Google Cloud Project or select an existing one</a></li>
          <li><a href="https://support.google.com/googleapi/answer/6158841" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Enable the Google Sheets API for your project</a></li>
          <li><a href="https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials#create_credentials_for_a_service_account" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Create service account credentials</a></li>
        </ol>

        <h4>3. Credential Configuration</h4>
        <p>Set up your credentials in your local environment:</p>
        <code>
          base64 -w 0 /path/to/your-service-account-creds.json
        </code>
        [For Linux users]
        <br />
        <code>
          base64 -b 0 -i /path/to/your-service-account-creds.json
        </code>
        [For MacOS users]
        <br />
        <code>
          echo 'export SHEET_CRED="paste-base64-output-here"' &gt;&gt; ~/.bashrc
        </code>
        <br />
        <code>
          source ~/.bashrc
        </code>

        <h4>4. Spreadsheet Access Configuration</h4>
        <ol>
          <li>Open your copied spreadsheet</li>
          <li>Click "Share" in the top right</li>
          <li>Add your service account email (ends with @developer.gserviceaccount.com)</li>
          <li>Grant "Editor" permissions</li>
          <li>Publish the spreadsheet:
            <ul>
              <li>File &gt; Share &gt; Publish to web</li>
              <li>Select "Comma-separated values (.csv)"</li>
              <li>Click "Publish"</li>
            </ul>
          </li>
        </ol>

        <h3>Working with the Integration Spreadsheet</h3>
        <p>Once your environment is set up, you can begin working with the spreadsheet:</p>

        <h4>1. Adding Your Model</h4>
        <p>The integration spreadsheet contains existing model definitions that serve as practical examples. You can either create a new entry following the patterns in existing rows, or practice by generating an existing model first to understand the process. Each row represents a complete model definition, use them as reference for creating a new row.</p>

        <h4>2. Generating the Model</h4>
        <p>Use mesheryctl to generate your models. Make sure to run the command inside your forked <code>meshery/meshery</code> repo</p>
        <code>mesheryctl registry generate --spreadsheet-id "YOUR_SPREADSHEET_ID" --spreadsheet-cred "$SHEET_CRED" --model "YOUR_MODEL_NAME"</code>

        <p>The command will:</p>
        <ul>
          <li>Read your spreadsheet data</li>
          <li>Validate the model definition</li>
          <li>Generate the model files</li>
          <li>For error logs your can checkout <code>~/.meshery/logs/registry/</code></li>
        </ul>

        <h4>3. Verification</h4>
        <p>The model will be generated in <code>meshery/server/meshmodels/[YOUR_MODEL_NAME]</code></p>

    <div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Using Meshery CLI with the Meshery Registry and Meshery Models</h4>
Meshery CLI has a set of commands that pertain to the lifecycle management of models:
    <br />

    - <code>mesheryctl registry</code> - interact with and update spreadsheets
    <br />
    - <code>mesheryctl models</code> - interact with and update Meshery Server
    <br />
    - <code>mesheryctl component</code> - interact with and update Meshery Server
    <br />
    - <code>mesheryctl relationships</code> - interact with and update Meshery Server
</div>


      </section>
  </div>
</section></div>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        }
      });
    });
  })();

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Edge Styles Guide</h1>
           <p>In Meshery, the line that connects <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/components">components</a> is called an <strong>edge</strong>. Each edge visually represents a <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/relationships">relationship</a> and uses a specific style to communicate its nature.</p>

<p>This guide helps you interpret the most common edge styles you will encounter.</p>

<h3 id="interpreting-common-edge-styles">Interpreting Common Edge Styles</h3>

<p>Meshery uses a set of default visual styles to provide at-a-glance information about the type of connection an edge represents. While these styles can be customized in the UI, understanding the defaults is key to interpreting component relationships.</p>

<h4 id="line-style-the-primary-indicator">Line Style: The Primary Indicator</h4>

<p>The line style is the most important visual cue for understanding an edge’s purpose.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Dotted Line</strong>:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>What it means</strong>: A <strong>semantic relationship</strong>. This represents a real, functional connection that Meshery understands and can manage, such as a network link or a volume mount.</li>
      <li><strong>When you’ll see it</strong>: These lines indicate active relationships between components, showing how they interact and communicate. The dotted pattern represents dynamic connections, while arrowheads show the direction of data flow or dependency.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Solid Line</strong>:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>What it means</strong>: A <strong>non-semantic annotation</strong>. This is a visual note or organizational aid for human interpretation only. Meshery’s engine ignores these connections.</li>
      <li><strong>When you’ll see it</strong>: These lines represent static or conceptual relationships between components. They help visualize structural connections or highlight specific component groupings without implying active data flow.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h4 id="color-a-secondary-cue">Color: A Secondary Cue</h4>

<p>Color provides an additional hint about an edge’s nature.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Green / Teal</strong>:
    <ul>
      <li>This is the default color for <strong>non-semantic annotations</strong>, helping them stand out from functional connections.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Blue / Grey</strong>:
    <ul>
      <li>These are the typical default colors for <strong>semantic relationships</strong>.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h3 id="edge-style-gallery">Edge Style Gallery</h3>

<p>The following gallery showcases the full range of visual styles available for edges in Meshery.</p>

<style>

     flex-direction: column;

<div class="extension-guides-container">

    
    
    
     
    
    

  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/ArrowHead.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Arrow Head</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Represents general direction or flow in diagrams. In UML, it could indicate direction in an association or dependency.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/BezierCurveLine.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Bezier Curve Line</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Used for curved relationships, which might indicate non-linear or non-direct connections. In UML, it could be used for inheritance or flow that isn't straightforward.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/FilledCircleHead.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Filled Circle Head</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Used for aggregation in UML, where one class contains another but does not own it (e.g., a library containing books).</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/FilledDiamondHead.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Filled Diamond Head</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Used for aggregation in UML, typically an empty diamond at the container end, indicating a "whole-part" relationship.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/FilledSquareHead.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Filled Square Head</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Represents composition in UML, a stronger relationship than aggregation, where the contained class cannot exist without the container (e.g., a house and its rooms).</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/FilledTriangleHead.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Filled Triangle Head</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Often used for inheritance in UML, where one class is a subclass of another. It indicates the "is-a" relationship.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/LineWithCircles.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Line With Circles</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Often represents a weak or indirect association in UML. It can also be used for dependencies or indicating optional relationships.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/SmoothLineWithCircle.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Smooth Line With Circle</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Represents a smooth transition or flow between elements. It could be used in scenarios where gradual change or influence is depicted.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/StraightLine.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Straight Line</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Represents a simple association or direct relationship between two entities or classes in UML.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/TreeLine.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Tree Line</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Represents hierarchical relationships, such as a parent class with child classes, or a main system branching into subsystems.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/WaveLine.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Wave Line</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Typically used to represent asynchronous signals or connections that aren't continuous. It may also denote complex relationships or uncertain flows in certain custom diagrams.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/ZigzagLine.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Zigzag Line</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>This is often used to represent signals with interference or noise. In system design, it can be used to indicate a disrupted or unreliable connection.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Exporting Models</h1>
           <p>Export existing Meshery <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a> or your custom infrastructure crd imported as <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a> in Meshery. The platform supports a variety of application definition formats, and you can export designs using either the Meshery CLI or the Meshery UI.</p>

<h2 id="export-models-using-meshery-cli">Export Models Using Meshery CLI</h2>

<p><strong>Step 1: Install Meshery CLI</strong></p>

<p>Before you can use the Meshery CLI to export a <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Model</a>, you must first install it. You can install Meshery CLI by <a href="/installation#install-mesheryctl">following the instructions</a>.</p>

<p><strong>Step 2: Export the Model</strong></p>

<p>Model can be exported in 2 format and OCI or Compress file. These files contain different <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">components</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">relationships</a> files and a model file. The files can be exported in either yaml or json by default it is exported as yaml.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model export [model-name] </div></div>
</pre>

<p>Different file type and output type can be set using flags <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-o</code> for oci and tar and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-t</code> for json or yaml. A location can also be specified using the -l flag where user needs to export the model</p>

<p><strong>Example :</strong></p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model export istio-base -o oci</div></div>
</pre>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model export istio-base -o oci -t json</div></div>
</pre>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> A <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--discard-components --discard-relationships</code> flag is present to skip <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">component</a> and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">relationships</a> generation in the export only the model is exported without any components and relationships.</p>

<h2 id="export-models-using-meshery-ui">Export Models Using Meshery UI</h2>

<p><strong>Step 1: Access the Meshery UI</strong></p>

<p>To Export a model into Meshery using the Meshery UI, you must first <a href="/v0.8/installation/quick-start">install Meshery</a></p>

<p><strong>Step 2: Navigate to Registry under Settings Page</strong></p>

<p>Once you have accessed the Meshery UI, navigate to the Registry under Settings. This page can be accessed by clicking on the Settings on the top right on setting icon and then selecting “Registry” and then choose model.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/export/Registry.png"><img alt="Registry-Navigator" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/export/Registry.png" /></a></p>

<p><strong>Step 3: Upload the Models</strong></p>

<p>On the Registry page, you can export your model by select Model in registry page. If no specific version the latest version is downloaded and if the specific version of model is selected then on clicking the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Export</code> button the model is exported as an OCI.</p>

<p>This Meshery model will include components, relationships.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/export/ExportModel.gif"><img alt="Export-Model" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/export/ExportModel.gif" /></a></p>

<p>Once the Meshery model has been exported, you can export your model anytime back using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Import</code> on UI and then visualize on , operate and observe your components that are geneated from the crd. You can also use Meshery to deploy your Meshery Model in form of a design to any of your connected kubernetes clusters. For more information, see <a href="/v0.8/installation/kubernetes">connections</a></p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        if (parentCollapse) {
          parentCollapse.classList.add("show");
        }
      });
    });
  })();

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Identifying Meshery Components</h1>
           <p>Ever wondered what the different icons and shapes in Meshery represent? Whether you’re looking at a dashboard, a settings page, or a design, you’ll encounter a rich library of visual elements. This guide is here to help you understand what they mean.</p>

<p>The <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/components">components</a> in Meshery fall into two fundamental categories, distinguished by whether they can be orchestrated (managed) by Meshery during deployment:</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Semantic Components (Orchestratable):</strong> These represent actual infrastructure resources that Meshery can understand and manage during deployment. Examples include Kubernetes resources (like Pods and Services), databases, and other infrastructure components. Meshery will actively manage their lifecycle during deployment.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Non-semantic Components (Annotation):</strong> These are visual elements used for documentation and organization, such as text boxes, arrows, shapes, and comments. Meshery ignores these during deployment as they don’t represent actual infrastructure.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Visual Customization</h4>
All components, whether semantic or non-semantic, support rich visual customization. For example, you can change the color of a Kubernetes Pod icon, modify its shape, or customize its background - it's all configurable!
</div>

<h2 id="semantic-components">Semantic Components</h2>

<p>These components represent real infrastructure that Meshery can manage. They can be either built-in (like Kubernetes components) or custom components that you <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/configuration-management/creating-models">create</a>.</p>

<h3 id="kubernetes-components">Kubernetes Components</h3>

<p>While Kubernetes components are commonly used, they follow the same principles as all other semantic components. They have a default distinct visual style to help you instantly recognize them:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Uniform Color Scheme:</strong> Kubernetes component icons typically use a <strong>distinctive blue background</strong> as a standard identifier.</li>
  <li><strong>Standardized Icon Structure:</strong> The fundamental structure is consistent: an outer container shape with the blue background, encompassing a unique inner white symbol.</li>
  <li><strong>Meaningful Inner Symbols:</strong> The white symbol inside each icon is the crucial unique identifier for that specific Kubernetes Kind, often inspired by the core function of the resource.</li>
</ul>

<p><a href="../../../assets/img/shapes/k8s_component.gif" target="_blank">
  <img src="../../../assets/img/shapes/k8s_component.gif" style="width:50%; height:auto;" alt="Kubernetes components in Meshery" />
</a></p>

<h3 id="integrated-technologies">Integrated Technologies</h3>

<p>Meshery supports various technologies (like AWS, Prometheus, Istio, KEDA, etc.) with their official icons. These components have the same orchestratable capabilities as Kubernetes components.</p>

<p><a href="../../../assets/img/shapes/AWS-models.png" target="_blank">
  <img src="../../../assets/img/shapes/AWS-models.png" style="width:50%; height:auto;" alt="AWS models in Meshery" />
</a></p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Exploring All Integrations</h4>
This guide covers the visual style of components. For a complete catalog of all technologies that Meshery integrates, visit the integrations directory. <strong><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensions/integrations">Explore All Integrations</a></strong>
</div>

<h2 id="non-semantic-components">Non-semantic Components</h2>

<p>These components help you document and organize your designs without affecting the actual infrastructure. They include:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Text boxes and comments for documentation</li>
  <li>Shapes and containers for visual grouping</li>
  <li>Lines and arrows for showing relationships</li>
  <li>Labels and tags for organization</li>
</ul>

<p>While these components are ignored during deployment, they support the same visual customization options as semantic components.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Edge Components</h4>
To learn more about edge components and their visual styles, visit the <strong><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensions/edges-shape-guide">Edge Components Guide</a></strong>
</div>

<h2 id="foundational-elements">Foundational Elements</h2>

<p>In addition to the rich library of predefined icons, Meshery also provides a core set of foundational geometric shapes. These are not tied to any specific technology but are intended for representing abstract concepts or for simple annotations within your designs where a specific component icon doesn’t apply.</p>

<p><a href="../../../assets/img/shapes/shapes.png" target="_blank">
  <img src="../../../assets/img/shapes/shapes.png" style="width:50%; height:auto;" alt="Generic shapes palette in Meshery" />
</a></p>

<details>
<summary><strong>Foundational Geometric Shapes</strong></summary>
<br />
These are the quintessential building blocks for many diagrams – your circles, squares, triangles, and basic polygons. They offer simple, clean, and universally understood forms for a wide range of uses.

<style>

  <div class="extension-guides-container">

    
    
    
     
    
    

  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Circle.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Circle</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>The default shape for nodes, displayed as an oval. This shape is useful for general-purpose nodes where no special distinction is required.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Heptagon.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Heptagon</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A polygon with seven straight sides and angles. This shape is less common but can be used to represent specific or unique data types that require distinction from other polygonal shapes.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Pentagon.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Pentagon</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A five-sided polygon often used for specific classifications of data. Its unique shape helps to quickly distinguish it from other polygonal shapes.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/RoundRectangle.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Round Rectangle</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>Similar to a rectangle but with rounded corners, providing a softer, more approachable look. This shape is often used to visually distinguish nodes from standard rectangular nodes, indicating a special status or different type of data.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/RoundTriangle.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Round Triangle</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A triangular shape with rounded corners, providing a softer look while still indicating hierarchy or direction.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Triangle.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Triangle</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A simple three-sided shape, often used to represent hierarchical data or directional flows. It is useful for indicating movement, direction, or hierarchical relationships within a network.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
   </div>


</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Common Representational &amp; Symbolic Shapes</strong></summary>
<br />
This group includes shapes that, by common convention, often evoke a more specific symbolic meaning, like using a "Barrel" for data storage or an "Actor" for a user role. Leveraging these established visual metaphors can make your custom diagrams more intuitive.

<style>

    .extension-guides-container {
      display: flex;
      flex-wrap: wrap;
      gap: 20px;
      justify-content: space-between;
      margin-top: 2rem;

     flex-direction: column;
       max-width: 20rem;
       max-height: 30rem;
       gap: 1rem;
  }
    .extension-guide-svg-container {
       height: auto;
       display: flex;
       flex-direction: column;
       align-items: center;
       gap: 0.455rem;
     flex-basis: 30%;

     height: auto;
  }

       display: flex;
       flex-direction: column;
       flex-basis: 77%;
       gap: 10px;
     text-align: center;
  }
