  <div class="extension-guides-container">

    
    
    
     
    
    

  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Barrel.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Barrel</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A shape resembling a 3D barrel, with both the top and bottom edges appearing rounded. This shape can be used to represent data storage, such as databases or repositories.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/GenericNode.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Generic Node</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A simple, often circular or rectangular shape used as a placeholder for unspecified or generic data points.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/RoundTag.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Round Tag</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A tag shape with rounded edges, offering a softer visual cue for categorized nodes.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Tag.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Tag</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A shape resembling a label or tag, useful for categorized or labeled data nodes.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/TextBox.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">TextBox</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A rectangular shape representing a text entry or display area, useful in diagrams to show nodes that contain text information or comments.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
   </div>


</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Specialized &amp; Decorative Geometric Shapes</strong></summary>
<br />
When your diagrams require a more distinct visual style or an element for emphasis, this collection offers a variety of options, from complex polygons to stylized forms like "Crescent," "Star," or "XWing." These shapes are less commonly used in Meshery and have no universally accepted meaning.

<style>

    .extension-guides-container {
      display: flex;
      flex-wrap: wrap;
      gap: 20px;
      justify-content: space-between;
      margin-top: 2rem;
  
    }

       display: flex;
     flex-direction: column;
       max-width: 20rem;
       max-height: 30rem;
       gap: 1rem;

    .extension-guide-svg-container {
       height: auto;
       display: flex;
       flex-direction: column;
       align-items: center;
       gap: 0.455rem;
     flex-basis: 30%;
  }
    .extension-guide-svg-container img {
     width: 50%;
     height: auto;
  }
    .extension-guide-details {
       display: flex;
       flex-direction: column;
       flex-basis: 77%;
       gap: 10px;
     text-align: center;
  }
    @media (max-width: 767px) {
      .extension-guide-container {
        flex-direction: column;
      }
      .extension-guide-svg-container {
        gap: 0.3rem;

        width: 40%;

        max-width: 30rem;
        flex-direction: column;
      }

  <div class="extension-guides-container">

    
    
    
     
    
    

  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/BottomRoundRectangle.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Bottom Round Rectangle</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A unique shape where only the bottom corners are rounded. This can be useful to indicate hierarchical relationships or to create a visual distinction from other rounded shapes.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/ConcaveHexagon.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Concave Hexagon</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A six-sided shape with one or more inward curves, creating a star-like appearance, useful for special types of nodes that need to stand out distinctly.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Crescent.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Crescent</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A shape resembling a crescent moon, which can be used to represent phases, growth, or transition nodes within a graph.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/CutRectangle.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Cut Rectangle</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A rectangle with corners that are cut off or beveled. This shape gives a more modern and distinct appearance, often used to highlight important nodes or different types of data.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Diamond.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Diamond</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A four-sided shape oriented at 45 degrees, resembling a diamond. It is typically used for decision points in flowcharts or to represent special conditions or states.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/LeftTriangle.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Left Triangle</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A triangular shape pointing to the left, often used to indicate directional flow or hierarchical steps in processes or data sequences.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Octagon.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Octagon</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>An eight-sided polygon, providing another option for representing complex data types. The additional sides make it stand out more compared to hexagons or pentagons.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Parallelogram.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Parallelogram</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A four-sided shape with opposite sides parallel, used to represent data processing steps or functions with directional flow.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Plus.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Plus(Polygon)</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A polygonal shape with any number of points, allowing for highly customizable node representations to fit specific data needs.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Polygon.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Polygon</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A custom point polygon allows the creation of irregular, user-defined polygonal shapes for graph nodes.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Rhomboid.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Rhomboid</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A quadrilateral with opposite sides parallel but not perpendicular, creating a skewed rectangle look. Useful for depicting relationships that aren't straightforward or direct.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/RightRhomboid.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Right Rhomboid</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A rhomboid where one angle is a right angle, offering a distinctive look for special types of data connections or relationships.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/RoundDiamond.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Round Diamond</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A diamond shape with rounded corners, used to indicate special conditions or decision points while maintaining a softer visual appeal.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/RoundHeptagon.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Round Heptagon</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A seven-sided polygon with rounded corners, less common but useful for unique data representations that require distinction.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/RoundHexagon.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Round Hexagon</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A six-sided polygon with rounded corners, providing a less angular look for complex data types.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/RoundOctagon.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Round Octagon</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>An eight-sided polygon with rounded corners, offering another distinct and less angular representation for complex data.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/SlantedParallelogram.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Slanted Parallelogram</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A four-sided shape with opposite sides parallel but slanted, creating a dynamic appearance often used to indicate processes or flows that have a directional aspect.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Star.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Star</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A shape with multiple points radiating outwards, typically used for highlighting special or notable nodes. It draws immediate attention, making it ideal for critical data points or focal nodes.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Trapezoid.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Trapezoid</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides, used to indicate hierarchical relationships or steps in a process.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/Vee.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">Vee</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>A shape resembling the letter "V", often used to show directionality or a splitting point in flowcharts.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
  
        <div class="extension-guide-card">
        <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/v0.8/assets/shapes/XWing.svg" alt="Edge" />
        
         <div style="text-align:center;">XWing</div>
        </div>
        <div class="extensino-guide-details">
        
        <div>This shape resembles the Star Wars X-Wing fighter, potentially useful for visually representing nodes that have multiple connections or interactions, symbolizing complexity and centrality.</div>
        
        
        </div>
        </div>
  
      
   </div>


</details>

</a></p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Importing Models</h1>
           <p>Import your existing Models and existing custom resource definition (CRD) into Meshery. The platform supports a variety of application definition formats, and you can import designs using either the Meshery CLI or the Meshery UI.</p>

<p><strong>Note:</strong> A <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Model</a> can be only imported if it contains atleast a valid <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Component</a> or <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationship</a>.</p>

<h2 id="import-models-using-meshery-cli">Import Models Using Meshery CLI</h2>

<div class="alert alert-warning">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Limitation on Importing Connections</h4>
The `mesheryctl model import` command currently supports importing Models containing Components, Relationships, and Policies. Importing Models with `Connection` definitions is not yet supported. This functionality may be added in a future release.
</div>

<p><strong>Step 1: Install Meshery CLI</strong></p>

<p>Before you can use the Meshery CLI to import a <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Model</a>, you must first install it. You can install Meshery CLI by <a href="/installation#install-mesheryctl">following the instructions</a>.</p>

<p><strong>Step 2: Import the Model</strong></p>

<p>Model can imported in 2 different format <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">URL, File</code>.The only cretiria for this import is the model should be a Meshery exported Model.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model import -f [file/url] </div></div>
</pre>

<p>The supported registrant are <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">github</code>,<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">artifacthub</code>.The URL format must be in this order.</p>

<p>https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/raw/refs/heads/main/filename</p>

<p><strong>Example :</strong></p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model import -f istio-base.tar</div></div>
</pre>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model import -f "https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/raw/refs/heads/main/filename"</div></div>
</pre>

<h2 id="import-models-using-meshery-ui">Import Models Using Meshery UI</h2>

<p><strong>Step 1: Access the Meshery UI</strong></p>

<p>To import a model into Meshery using the Meshery UI, you must first <a href="/v0.8/installation/quick-start">install Meshery</a></p>

<p><strong>Step 2: Navigate to Registry under Settings Page</strong></p>

<p>Once you have accessed the Meshery UI, navigate to the Registry under Settings. This page can be accessed by clicking on the Settings on the top right on setting icon and then selecting “Registry” and then choose model.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/export/Registry.png"><img alt="Registry-Navigator" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/export/Registry.png" /></a></p>

<p><strong>Step 3: Upload the Model</strong></p>

<p>On the Registry page, you can import your model clicking the import button in registry page. Selecting URL or File and then hitting Import</p>

<p>This Meshery model will include components, relationships.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/import/ImportModel.gif"><img alt="Import-Model" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/import/ImportModel.gif" /></a></p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });

          <h1>Cloud Native Design Patterns</h1>
           <div class="alert alert-warning">
<h4 class="alert-heading">What are Cloud Native Patterns?</h4>
This feature area is under active development. Patterns will be importable and exportable as OCI images in v0.8.0.
</div>

<p>Patterns are essentially atomic designs with one or more components made in composed into an atomic, reusable design. Patterns are a way to apply the DRY principle when managing the configuration of cloud native infrastructure.</p>

<h2 id="use-meshery-to-deploy-a-cloud-native-pattern">Use Meshery to Deploy a Cloud Native Pattern</h2>

<p>Use Meshery to deploy a cloud native pattern. Cloud native patterns are detailed as a YAML file. See the <a href="/v0.8/guides/configuration-management">Configuration Management</a> guide.</p>

<h3 id="pattern-repository">Pattern Repository</h3>

<p><em>See <a href="https://meshery.io/catalog">Meshery Catalog</a></em>.</p>

<p>You may bring your own patterns or find them available through your chosen provider. Each cloud native pattern carries a unique identifier for reference. The patterns in this repository serve in an educational capacity, facilitating learning, and also serve in an operational capacity, facilitating implementation and validation of your cloud native deployment’s adherence to a pattern.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Repository of Cloud Native Patterns</h4>
A central set of design patterns is available in Meshery Catalog (<a href="/v0.8/concepts/catalog">concept</a>, <a href="https://meshery.io/catalog">site</a>).
</div>

<h2 id="importing-patterns">Importing Patterns</h2>

<p>You can import a pattern using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> or Meshery UI. Patterns can be imported from your local filesystem, an HTTP/S endpoint, or from GitHub. When provided a GitHub location (org/repo), Meshery will recursively search the given directory (or the entire repository) for existing pattern files.</p>

<h3 id="using-meshery-cli">Using Meshery CLI</h3>

<h4 id="to-import-a-pattern-execute-this-command">To import a pattern, execute this command:</h4>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>$ mesheryctl design import -f &lt;path to the pattern&gt;
Importing pattern…
Pattern imported.
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="using-meshery-ui">Using Meshery UI:</h3>

<p>From Meshery UI, patterns can be imported from your local filesystem or imported from a remote URL.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/patterns/ImportPatternUI.png">
    <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/patterns/ImportPatternUI.png" style="width: 60%" />
</a></p>

<p><em>To upload from url click the link icon</em></p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/patterns/UrlImport.png">
    <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/patterns/UrlImport.png" style="width: 60%" />
</a></p>

<h4 id="to-deploy-a-pattern-execute-this-command">To deploy a pattern, execute this command:</h4>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>$ mesheryctl design apply -f &lt;path to the pattern&gt;
Deploying pattern…
Pattern successfully applied.
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>From here, output and behavior will vary based upon the specific pattern you’re deploying. Should you find that your pattern is not successfully deployed, refer to the pattern troubleshooting guide in the Meshery documentation.</p>

<p>As you step through each pattern, you might choose to modify the pattern to suit your specific environment and workload, exploring in-context of your specific situation. Optionally, you may choose to use a plugin like , or another visual cloud native topology tool, to facilitate your comprehension of the patterns and to literally see the patterns in-action.</p>

<p>Take time to explore. Try deploying one cloud native’s sample application onto a different cloud native and compare differences in behavior and each cloud native’s ability to manage it. If using Meshery to do so, execute the following commands as an example to deploy the sample application, BookCatalog, onto Open cloud native:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>$ mesheryctl design apply -f book-catalog
Deploying application “BookCatalog”...
Deployed. Endpoint(s) available at: http://localhost:8000/catalog
</code></pre></div></div>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Configuring your Cloud Native Infrastructure and Applications</h1>
           <p>As an cloud native management platform, Meshery has built-in support infastructure and application configuration management. Use Meshery to configure your multi-cluster Kubernetes environments on-premises or across clouds.</p>

<h2 id="what-is-a-meshery-design">What is a Meshery Design?</h2>

<p>Meshery’s core construct of configuration management is that of a design. A design is ultimately a document – and a document in which you capture and describe your desired state of improv the environment.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/patterns/context-aware-design.svg"><img src="/assets/img/patterns/context-aware-design.svg" alt="Context Aware Design" /></a></p>

<h2 id="creating-a-meshery-design">Creating a Meshery Design</h2>

<p>You have your choice of how are you would like to create an infrastructure design. You can use the design configurator inside of measure, UI or extensions, like , or you can hand code your design, using the mesh model spec, if you like.</p>

<p>You are free to choose how you would like to create an infrastructure design. You can use the design configurator inside of measure, UI or extensions, like , or you can hand code your design, using the mesh model spec, if you like.</p>

<p>Use Meshery UI or mesheryctl to create designs.</p>

<h2 id="pattern-management-through-meshery-ui">Pattern Management Through Meshery UI</h2>

<p>Meshery also comes with seed patterns when users start Meshery for the first time. These patterns cover common use cases and examples for you as you explore Meshery.</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/configuration-management/meshery-patterns.png" width="50%" /></p>

<p>Users can also import these patterns to their remote provider from this <a href="https://github.com/service-mesh-patterns/service-mesh-patterns/tree/master/samples">sample repository</a>.</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/configuration-management/pattern-import.png" width="50%" /></p>

<p>Once these patterns are imported, you can then edit these patterns or use the pattern configurator to configure them according to your requirements.</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/configuration-management/pattern-configure-button.png" width="50%" /></p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/configuration-management/pattern-configure.png" width="50%" /></p>

<h2 id="pattern-management-through-meshery-cli">Pattern Management Through Meshery CLI</h2>

<p>You can also manage cloud native patterns through Meshery’s CLI, mesheryctl.</p>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl design</code> subcommand lets you import and apply patterns to your cluster.</p>

<p>For example, if you have your pattern written in a file say, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">istio-bookinfo.yaml</code> which deploys Istio service mesh and onboards the BookInfo app on Istio, you can use mesheryctl to apply this pattern as shown below:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl design apply -f istio-bookinfo.yaml
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If you already have a pattern imported into Meshery, you can apply the pattern by name.</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl design apply BookInfoApp
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This will apply the pattern BookInfoApp, which has already been imported into Meshery.</p>

<p>See <a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/#cloud-native-pattern-configuration-and-management">mesheryctl design subcommand section</a> for more details on the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">design</code> subcommand.</p>

<h2 id="wasm-filters">WASM Filters</h2>

<p>Meshery can be used for managing WebAssembly Filters through the UI or the CLI.</p>

<h3 id="filter-management-through-meshery-ui">Filter Management Through Meshery UI</h3>

<p>Like patterns, Meshery also comes with some sample WebAssembly Filters for you to experiment.</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/configuration-management/meshery-filters.png" width="50%" /></p>

<p>You can also import these filters manually to your provider from the <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/wasm-filters">wasm-filters</a> repo.</p>

<p>Meshery’s sample application <a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">ImageHub</a> will let you test out configuring these filters out-of-the-box.</p>

<p>You can onboard ImageHub to an installed service mesh as shown below.</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/configuration-management/image-hub.png" width="50%" /></p>

<h3 id="filter-management-through-meshery-cli">Filter Management Through Meshery CLI</h3>

<p>You can also manage WASM filters through Meshery’s CLI, mesheryctl.</p>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl filter</code> command lets you import and configure WebAssembly filters.</p>

<p>For example,</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl exp filter apply -f metrics_collector_bg.wasm
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If you already have a filter imported into Meshery, you can configure the filter by name.</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl exp filter apply metrics_collector_bg
</code></pre></div></div>
   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

      <ul class="section-title">
          
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/deploy-azure-resources-with-meshery">Deploy Azure resources with Meshery</a>
            
              -  Learn how to deploy and manage Azure resources through Kubernetes with Meshery, utilizing ASO operator to enhance cloud resource management
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/deploy-aws-ec2-instances-with-meshery">Deploy AWS EC2 Instances with Meshery</a>
            
              -  Learn how to deploy and manage AWS EC2 instances through Kubernetes with Meshery, utilizing AWS Controllers for Kubernetes (ACK) to enhance cloud resource management
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/deploy-azure-storage-account-with-meshery">Deploy Azure Storage Account with Meshery</a>
            
              -  Learn how to deploy and manage Azure Storage account through Kubernetes with Meshery, utilizing ASO operator to enhance cloud resource management
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/deploy-apache-cassandra-with-statefulset">Deploying Apache Cassandra with a StatefulSet in Meshery Playground</a>
            
              -  Deploy Apache Cassandra with a StatefulSet using Meshery Playground in an interactive live cluster environment.
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/deploy-php-redis">Deploying PHP Guestbook application with Redis in Meshery</a>
            
              -  In this tutorial, we will deploy guest book built with PHP and Redis in Kubernetes. We will make use of Meshery Playground in an interactive live cluster environment.
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/embedding-meshery-design-in-wordpress">Embedding a Meshery Design in a WordPress Post</a>
            
              -  Learn how to Embed a Meshery Design in a WordPress Post
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/exploring-kubernetes-cronjobs">Exploring Kubernetes CronJobs</a>
            
              -  In this tutorial, we will explore how to use Meshery Playground, an interactive live cluster environment, to perform hands-on labs for managing Kubernetes CronJobs.
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/kubernetes-services">Exploring Kubernetes Services with Meshery</a>
            
              -  Explore Kubernetes Services using Meshery using Meshery Playground, an interactive live environment, through a series of hands-on exercises.
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials">Tutorials</a>
            
              -  Explore the tutorials to learn how to use Meshery for collaboratively managing infrastructure.
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/kubernetes-configmaps-secrets">Understanding Kubernetes ConfigMaps and Secrets with Meshery</a>
            
              -  In this tutorial, we will explore how to effectively use Kubernetes ConfigMaps and Secrets for managing configuration data and sensitive information. Leveraging Meshery Playground, an interactive live cluster environment, we'll perform hands-on labs to understand the practical aspects of working with ConfigMaps and Secrets in Kubernetes.
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/kubernetes-deployments">Exploring Kubernetes Deployments with Meshery</a>
            
              -  Explore a Kubernetes Deployment using Meshery Playground, an interactive live environment, through a series of hands-on exercises.
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/kubernetes-pods">Exploring Kubernetes Pods with Meshery</a>
            
              -  Explore Kubernetes Pods using Meshery in an interactive live cluster environment, through a series of hands-on exercises.
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/kubernetes-request-flow">Kubernetes Request Flow – A Visual Guide</a>
            
              -  A visual walkthrough of how user requests flow through Kubernetes components using Meshery .
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/publish-to-artifacthub">Publishing Meshery Designs to ArtifactHub</a>
            
              -  Step by step example for how to export Meshery Designs and publish them to an ArtifactHub repository.
            
            </li>
            
          
          <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/wordpress-mysql-persistentvolume">Deploying WordPress and MySQL with Persistent Volumes with Meshery</a>
            
              -  Deploy a WordPress site and a MySQL database with Persistent Volumes using Meshery Playground in an interactive live cluster environment.
            
            </li>
            
          
      </ul>

          <h1>Envoy WASM Filter Management</h1>
           <p>Meshery offers powerful features that simplify the management of Envoy WASM filters in Istio.</p>

<h3 id="meshery-ui-and-cli-integration">Meshery UI and CLI Integration</h3>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Import WASM Envoy Filters</strong>: Easily import your WebAssembly Envoy filters into Meshery using the intuitive UI or the command-line interface (<a href="https://docs.meshery.io/reference/mesheryctl#data-plane-intelligence">CLI</a>).</li>
  <li><strong>Publish and Clone Filters</strong>: Share your filters with the community by publishing them in the <a href="https://meshery.io/catalog">Meshery Catalog</a> and make it effortless for others to clone them.</li>
  <li><strong>Download WASM Binaries</strong>: Access and download WebAssembly binaries directly from your Remote Provider like <a href="https://cloud.meshery.io/">Meshery Cloud</a>.</li>
  <li><strong>Efficient Data Plane Design</strong>: Seamlessly design and deploy Istio and Envoy data planes using extensions like .</li>
  <li><strong>Contribute to Open Source</strong>: Get involved with the cloud native community by contributing to any of the open source <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/wasm-filters">wasm-filters</a> developed by the Meshery community.</li>
</ul>

<p><img src="https://mcusercontent.com/6b50be5aea3dfe1fd4c041d80/images/a07ef29a-4cf8-986e-9bd3-78db7dc00ce1.png" width="100px" style="float:left;position:relative;margin: 1rem 1rem 1rem 0rem" /></p>

<h2 id="envoy-wasm-filter-management">Envoy WASM Filter Management</h2>

<p>As of Meshery v0.7, the management of Envoy WASM filters includes:</p>

<p><strong>Meshery Server Integration</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>✅ New WASM Filter Component: A new component is available in the Design Configurator to simplify filter management.</li>
  <li>✅ Improved Component Icon: Enhancements have been made to provide a more user-friendly experience.</li>
  <li>✅ Relationship Patch Policy: A new policy has been introduced to streamline the relationship between components.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Meshery CLI</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>✅ Import Filters: Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl filter import [URL | filepath]</code> to effortlessly import filters.</li>
  <li>✅ Delete Filters: Remove unwanted filters with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl filter delete [filter-name | ID]</code>.</li>
  <li>✅ View Filters: Gain insights into your filters using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl filter view [filter-name | ID]</code>.</li>
  <li>✅ List and Search Filters: Easily navigate filters with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl filter list [filter-name | ID]</code>.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong> Integration</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>✅ Apply WASM Filters: Hierarchically apply filters to your Envoy configurations.</li>
  <li>✅ Deploy/Undeploy Filters: Streamline the deployment and removal of filters with custom configurations.</li>
  <li>✅ Enhanced Visibility: View filters within a dedicated panel and seamlessly drop them onto the canvas.</li>
</ul>

<p><img src="https://mcusercontent.com/6b50be5aea3dfe1fd4c041d80/images/1e9c2e71-1b3e-a132-4766-8cefdc9861d2.png" width="50px" style="float:left;position:relative;margin: 1rem 1rem 1rem 0rem" /></p>

<p><strong>Meshery UI Enhancements</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>✅ Import Filters: Import filters directly via URL or filesystem.</li>
  <li>✅ Improved Browsing: Browse, search, and view filters in both grid view and table view.</li>
  <li>✅ Streamlined Lists: Easily list and search filters in grid view or table view.</li>
  <li>✅ Download Filters: Download filters effortlessly from the UI.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Remote Provider and Meshery Catalog Integration</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>✅ Permanent Storage and Artifact Dispersal: Ensure your filters are securely stored and widely accessible.</li>
  <li>✅ Catalog Features: Import, clone, download, publish, and unpublish filters within the Meshery Catalog.</li>
  <li>✅ Enhanced Privacy Controls: Manage user permissions, team ownership, and visibility for your filters.</li>
  <li>✅ Content Curation: Streamline content curation with an approval flow request queue.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="performance-management-upgrades">Performance Management Upgrades</h2>

<p>In addition to Envoy WASM filter management, we’ve also introduced new performance management features:</p>

<p><strong>Meshery Server</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>✅ Performance Profiles: Tailor your performance profiles to match your specific needs.</li>
  <li>✅ SSL Certificate Support: Benefit from SSL certificate support for Fortio in the server.</li>
  <li>✅ Performance Analysis Comparison: Compare performance with and without filters.</li>
  <li>✅ GetNighthawk and Cloud Native Performance Releases: Access the latest releases of GetNighthawk and Cloud Native Performance.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Meshery CLI</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>✅ Performance Profile Flags: Specify additional load generator flags with performance profiles.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Meshery UI</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>✅ Performance Profile Flags: Customize load generator flags directly in the UI.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Service Performance Project</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>✅ Define Performance Profiles: Clearly define your performance profiles.</li>
  <li>✅ Dashboard Integration: Display test results on the dashboard.</li>
  <li>✅ Intel Integration: Incorporate Intel design into scheduled workflows for Istio.</li>
  <li>✅ Consolidated Performance Profiles: Streamline performance profiles on the dashboard.</li>
</ul>

<p>Meshery offers WebAssembly-based network traffic management filters in Envoy, bringing a new level of flexibility and control to your Istio deployments.</p>

<h2 id="frequently-asked-questions">Frequently Asked Questions</h2>

<h3 id="q-why-does-meshery-provide-and-manage-wasm-filters">Q: Why does Meshery provide and manage WASM filters?</h3>

<p>Meshery manages WASM filters for data plane proxies for:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Agility</strong>: in partnership with service mesh control planes, Meshery can dynamically load, configure, and unload filter(s) in running Envoy proxies.</li>
  <li><strong>Maintainability</strong>: To extend the functionality we don’t have to change the entire codebase.</li>
  <li><strong>Diversity</strong> : WASM filters can be easily compiled with many popular programming languages like C/C++ and Rust.</li>
  <li><strong>Reliability and isolation</strong> : WASM filters are deployed into VM and hence they are isolated from the Envoy process. For instance if the WASM filter crashes it will not impact the envoy process.</li>
  <li><strong>Security</strong> : The WASM filter uses a well defined API to connect with the host i.e envoy proxy which can be modified only a limited number of connections.</li>
  <li><strong>Speed</strong> : It is originally used to speed up large web application</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="q-what-is-envoy-proxy">Q: What is Envoy proxy?</h3>

<p>An <strong>Envoy</strong> is a high performance, programmable L3/L4 and L7 proxy that a number of service mesh use as their data plane. Connection and request handling are at the core of Envoy’s focus. Envoy’s has a pluggable filter module that allows the incorporation of WebAssembly filters that provide additional traffic filtering intelligence. Often this includes higher order functions such as access control, transformation, data enrichment, auditing and more.</p>

<h3 id="q-what-is-wasm-">Q: What is WASM ?</h3>

<p>WebAssembly is a low-level assembly-like language with a compact binary format that runs with near-native performance and provides languages such as C/C++, C# and Rust with a compilation target so that they can run in many different environments, including behind Envoy’s Application Binary Interface to extend Envoy with new capabilities. WASM programs are distributed in an efficient portable binary instruction format and embed into isolated execution environments.</p>

<h3 id="q-what-are-the-disadvantages-of-wasm-filters-to-be-taken-into-consideration">Q: What are the disadvantages of WASM filters to be taken into consideration?</h3>

<p>Execution of WASM filters requires system resources. Just as executing the same functionality that your filter provides outside of the WASM virtual machine, resources can include overhead of latency, CPU, and memory. See the <a href="https://smp-spec.io">Cloud Native Performance</a> project for more detail.</p>

<h3 id="q-what-is-the-envoy-proxy-wasm-sdk">Q: What is the Envoy Proxy WASM SDK?</h3>

<p>Envoy proxy runs the WASM filter in a stack-based virtual machine so that the filter memory is isolated from the host environment. The interaction between the embedded host i.e. Envoy proxy and the WASM filter are done via call backs and functions by the Envoy Proxy WASM SDK. The Envoy Proxy WASM SDK is implemented in various programming languages like C++, RUST, AssemblyScript and GO(still experimental)</p>

<h3 id="q-what-is-image-hub-">Q: What is Image Hub ?</h3>

<p>Image Hub is a sample application which was first officially demonstrated at DockerCon 2020. This sample application is written to run on consul to explore the WebAssembly (WASM) modules in the Envoy filter. This application is written in the RUST programming language. These modules are used to implement the multi-tenancy or to implement the per user rate limiting in the applications endpoint.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>GitOps with Meshery</h1>
           <h2 id="--snapshot-github-action"><img style="height: 4rem; width: 4rem;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/-icon-color.svg" />  Snapshot GitHub Action</h2>

<ul>
  <li>See your deployment before you merge</li>
  <li>Connect  to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request</li>
  <li>Get snapshots of your infrastructure directly in your PRs</li>
</ul>

<h3>Using Meshery's SnapShot GitHub Action</h3>
<p>See your deployment before you merge. Connect  to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request. Get snapshots of your infrastructure directly in your PRs.</p>

<p>See <a href="/v0.8/extensions/snapshot">Extension:  Snapshot</a> for more details.</p>

<h2 id="-meshery-performance-analysis-github-action"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/smp-dark-text-side.svg" classname="image-left-no-shadow" alt="Infrastructure fperformance logo" style="width: 60%; max-width: 200px;vertical-align:middle" /> Meshery Performance Analysis GitHub Action</h2>

<ul>
  <li>See your performance regressions before you merge</li>
  <li>Connect Performance Management to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request</li>
  <li>Red light performance regressions</li>
  <li>Baseline and analyze the performance of your services is key to efficient operation of any application
    <ul>
      <li>Meshery is the canonical implementation of the Cloud Native Performance specification</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Define your performance profiles upfront. See statistical analysis with microservice latency and throughput quartiles</li>
  <li>Meshery includes your choice of load generator, so that you can meausure your way</li>
  <li>Meshery packages all these features into an easy-to-use GitHub Action</li>
</ul>

<p>Measuring and managing the performance of your infrastructure is key to efficient operation. You can choose from multiple load generators and use a highly configurable set of load profiles with variable tunable facets to run a performance test. Meshery packages all these features into an easy-to-use GitHub Action.</p>

<h3>Using Meshery's Performance Analysis GitHub Action</h3>

<p>The <a href="https://github.com/marketplace/actions/performance-testing-with-meshery">Meshery Performance Analysis GitHub Action</a> is available in the GitHub Marketplace. You can create your own performance profiles to run repeatable tests with Meshery. You can configure this action to trigger with each of your releases, on every pull request or any GitHub workflow trigger event. A sample configuration of the action is shown below.</p>

<div class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Meshery SMP Action</span>
<span class="na">on</span><span class="pi">:</span>
  <span class="na">push</span><span class="pi">:</span>
    <span class="na">branches</span><span class="pi">:</span>
      <span class="s1">'</span><span class="s">master'</span>

<span class="na">jobs</span><span class="pi">:</span>
  <span class="na">performance-test</span><span class="pi">:</span>
    <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Performance Test</span>
    <span class="na">runs-on</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">ubuntu-latest</span>
    <span class="na">steps</span><span class="pi">:</span>
      <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">checkout</span>
        <span class="na">uses</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">actions/checkout@v2</span>
        <span class="na">with</span><span class="pi">:</span>
          <span class="na">ref</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s1">'</span><span class="s">perf'</span>

      <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Deploy k8s-minikube</span>
        <span class="na">uses</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">manusa/actions-setup-minikube@v2.4.1</span>
        <span class="na">with</span><span class="pi">:</span>
          <span class="na">minikube version</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s1">'</span><span class="s">v1.21.0'</span>
          <span class="na">kubernetes version</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s1">'</span><span class="s">v1.20.7'</span>
          <span class="na">driver</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">docker</span>

      <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Run Performance Test</span>
        <span class="na">with</span><span class="pi">:</span>
          <span class="na">provider_token</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">$</span>
          <span class="na">platform</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">docker</span>
          <span class="na">profile_name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">soak-test</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>You can also define your test configuration in an SMP compatible configuration file as shown below.</p>

<div class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="na">smp_version</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">v0.0.1</span>
<span class="na">id</span><span class="pi">:</span>
<span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Istio Performance Test</span>
<span class="na">labels</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="pi">{}</span>
<span class="na">clients</span><span class="pi">:</span>
<span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">internal</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="no">false</span>
  <span class="na">load_generator</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">fortio</span>
  <span class="na">protocol</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="m">1</span>
  <span class="na">connections</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="m">2</span>
  <span class="na">rps</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="m">10</span>
  <span class="na">headers</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="pi">{}</span>
  <span class="na">cookies</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="pi">{}</span>
  <span class="na">body</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="s">"</span>
  <span class="na">content_type</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="s">"</span>
  <span class="na">endpoint_urls</span><span class="pi">:</span>
  <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="s">http://localhost:2323/productpage</span>
<span class="na">duration</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="s">30m"</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>See this sample GitHub workflow (<a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-smp-action/blob/master/action.yml">action.yml</a>) for more configuration details.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/service-mesh-performance-profile-test-results.png"><img src="/assets/img/service-mesh-performance-profile-test-results.png" classname="image-center" alt="performance management dashboard" /></a></p>

<p>The results from the tests are updated on the Performance Management dashboard in Meshery. To learn more about interpreting the test results, check out <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/performance-management/interpreting-performance-test-results">this guide</a>. You can always checkout the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides">Meshery User Guides</a> to dive deep into these features.</p>

<p><a href="https://smp-spec.io">Cloud Native Performance</a> standardizes infrastructure measurement, characterizing any deployment’s performance by capturing the details of infrastructure capacity, configuration and workload metadata.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Infrastructure Management Guides</h1>
           <p>Guides for understanding Meshery’s ability to manage infrastructure.</p>

<ul class="section-title">
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">Deploying Sample Applications</a>
    
        -  This guide is to help users get a better understanding of sample apps
    
    </li>
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/notification-management">Managing Events with Notification Center</a>
    
        -  Meshery tracks operations performed on your infrastructure and workloads, and provides notification of environment issues, application conflicts with infrastructure configuration, policy violations, and so on.
    
    </li>
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/filter-management">Envoy WASM Filter Management</a>
    
        -  Meshery provides the ability to manage WASM filters for data plane proxies for agility, maintainability, diversity, reliability and isolation, security, and speed.
    
    </li>
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/gitops-with-meshery">GitOps with Meshery</a>
    
        -  Integrating your CI/CD pipelines with Meshery's GitHub Actions
    
    </li>
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/registering-a-connection">Infrastructure Discovery</a>
    
        -  MeshSync supports both greenfield and brownfield discovery of infrastructure. Greenfield discovery manages infrastructure created and managed entirely by Meshery, while brownfield discovery identifies separately created infrastructure.
    
    </li>
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/overview">Infrastructure Management</a>
    
        -  Meshery provides the ability to manage infrastructure for agility, maintainability, diversity, reliability and isolation, security, and speed.
    
    </li>
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/lifecycle-management">Managing Connections</a>
    
        -  Manage the lifecycle of your infrastructure by registering each infrastructure element with Meshery.
    
    </li>
