$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Managing Connections</h1>
           <p><a name="lifecycle-management"></a></p>

<p>Meshery manages hundreds of different types of cloud native infrastructure. See the <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/integrations">full set of integrations</a>.</p>

<h2 id="cloud-native-infrastructure-lifecycle-management">Cloud Native Infrastructure Lifecycle Management</h2>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/lifecycle-management/states-for-kubernetes-cluster-connections.svg"><img src="/assets/img/lifecycle-management/states-for-kubernetes-cluster-connections.svg" alt="Lifecycle Management" /></a></p>

<p>Meshery Adapters can optionally be deployed to provide deep support of different types of infrastructure, so that you can learn and compare different infrastructure functionality. Once you have selected to operate a given infrastructure, Meshery will assist you with ongoing operations.</p>

<p>Meshery automates the provisioning of various infrastructurees, allowing users to select different configuration profiles in order to support a variety of deployment models.</p>

<p>Meshery adapters will dynamically retrieve the specific infrastructure’s release package upon initial deployment of a given infrastructure. Meshery adapters cache (in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery/bin</code>) the infrastructure installation package.</p>

<h4 id="deprovisioning-infrastructure">Deprovisioning infrastructure</h4>

<p>Just as Meshery automates the provisioning of various cloud native infrastructure, so too does it facilitate the deprovisioning of infrastructure. Find the “Undeploy” button in Meshery UI or the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--undeploy</code> flag in Meshery CLI.</p>

<h2 id="workload-lifecycle-management">Workload Lifecycle Management</h2>

<p>Users may bring their applications (perform workload onboarding) on the infrastructure using the Custom Configuration operation.</p>

<p>Commonly adjoining each infrastructure is a sample application that facilitates demonstration of the value of the given infrastructure. Meshery allows you to efficiently <a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">install sample applications</a> across different infrastructurees.</p>

<h2 id="configuration-management">Configuration Management</h2>

<p>Meshery provides the ability for you as a infrastructure manager to customize your infrastructure deployment.</p>

<h2 id="notifications">Notifications</h2>

<p>Meshery tracks operations that you perform on infrastructurees and their workloads. Meshery provides notification of environment issues, application conflicts with infrastructure configuration, and so on.</p>

<h4 id="acknowledging-and-dismissing-notifications">Acknowledging and dismissing notifications</h4>

<p>Depending upon the severity of the notification, many notifications are informational and can readily be dismissed after reading. Some notifications include actionable alerts. Learn more in “<a href="/v0.8/guides/events-management">Managing Events with Notification Center</a>”.</p>

<h2 id="lifecycle-faqs">Lifecycle FAQs</h2>

<details>
<summary>
<strong>Question:</strong> “Meshery is a collaboration platform. When I bring my infrastructure under Meshery's management, will my Kubernetes clusters be available to all other users? Can other people access my cluster?
</summary><strong>Answer:</strong> <p>Yes, they can, <i>IF</i> you explicitly allow them to do so. It's important to understand the following controls and system behavior:</p>
<p><b>1. Ownership:</b> Every connection to a Kubernetes cluster is created by and owned by the individual that provided the Kubernetes context. That individual may elect to share the connection with others on their team (if you have invited anyone to your team(s)).</p>
<p><b>2. Permission:</b> If you do grant other team members access, you do so by creating an environment, assigning that Kubernetes connection to the environment, then creating a workspace and assigning that environment to the workspace. Users of any of your teams to which you have shared access to the workspace will then have permission to access the cluster.</p>
<p><b>3. Connectivity:</b> those individuals will have to be afforded network connectivity to that cluster (in whatever fashion you deem appropriate). Grossly, there are two ways in which this can occur:</p>
<p>3.a) The other user runs their own copy of Meshery (or signs into a shared instance like the Playground) and will see the connection as being available when they sign in. Their Meshery Server will need to be able to reach your Kube API over the network. How that is done can be any number of ways and is left unto your own devices.</p>
<p>3.b.) The other user signs into your Meshery Server instance, which has network access to your Kubernetes cluster. In order for the other user to sign into your Meshery Server, you would have to expose it to the Internet or VPN or… one of the many other ways to all them access to your Meshery Server.</p>
<p>So, in short, yes, you can share access to your Kubernetes cluster with other users, but you have to explicitly grant them access to do so. For more information please visit <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/authorization">Remote Provider Permissions</a>.</p>
</details>

<div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Discussion Forum</h4>
Don't find an answer to your question here? Ask on the <a href="https://discuss.meshery.io">Discussion Forum</a>.
</div>

$(document).ready(function() {

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });

        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Managing Events with Notification Center</h1>
           <p>Meshery continuously tracks activities affecting your infrastructure and workloads. Meshery generates a variety of events, reflecting activities affecting the design and operation of your infrastructure whether those activities are directly or indirectly performed through Meshery operations.</p>

<h3 id="what-is-the-notification-center">What is the Notification Center?</h3>
<p>The Notification Center is a dedicated panel in Meshery’s UI that helps you monitor, understand, and respond to events across your system. It acts as a central place where you can see important updates related to your infrastructure, workloads, and Meshery’s internal operations.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/find-notification-center.gif">
  <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/find-notification-center.gif" alt="Notification Position" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a></p>

<h3 id="types-of-notifications">Types of Notifications</h3>

<p>Given the variety of activities that occur through the process of managing infrastructure, notifications have been grouped into categories so that you can readily understand what a notification means and what do to about any particular type you have received.</p>

<p>Each notification in Meshery includes a clear summary of what occurred in your system. Notifications vary in format depending on the event type, but typically include:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Action performed (e.g., saved a design, ran a dry run)</li>
  <li>Affected components (e.g., deployments, MeshSync, events)</li>
  <li>Validation results or errors (e.g., invalid values, missing fields)</li>
  <li>Relationship updates (e.g., how components are linked)</li>
  <li>Links to the related design or further details</li>
</ul>

<p>You can mark notifications as read or unread to stay organized and focused. Meshery highlights critical, actionable events in red, helping you quickly spot and respond to urgent issues.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/description.png">
  <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/description.png" alt="Event Descriptions" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a></p>

<blockquote>
  <p>🔗 For more technical details, see the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center">Contributor Reference</a>.</p>
</blockquote>

<h3 id="notification-timestamps">Notification Timestamps</h3>
<p>Each notification includes a timestamp showing when the event happened. The time is displayed based on your local device’s time zone, so it reflects your current time.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/timestamps.png">
  <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/timestamps.png" alt="Notification Timestamps" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a></p>

<h3 id="data-sharing">Data Sharing</h3>
<p>Need to collaborate?
You can share notifications with teammates or stakeholders in just a few clicks — making it easier to communicate and resolve issues.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/notification-share.png">
  <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/notification-share.png" alt="Notification Share" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a></p>

<h3 id="filtering-and-searching">Filtering and Searching</h3>

<p>The Notification Center provides a powerful way to filter and search through events. You can narrow down results using filters such as <strong>severity</strong>, <strong>status</strong>, <strong>action</strong>, <strong>category</strong>, and <strong>author</strong>.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Note: Some filter options such as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">action</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">category</code>, and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">author</code> are dynamically generated based on the notifications your Meshery instance has received. These values are retrieved from the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/api/system/events/types</code> endpoint.</p>
</blockquote>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/notification-filter.gif">
  <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/notification-filter.gif" alt="Notification Filter" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a></p>

<h4 id="severity">Severity</h4>

<p>Filter notifications based on the level of severity, indicated by icon color and symbol. These levels are defined in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SEVERITY</code> constant and styled using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SEVERITY_STYLE</code>.</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Level</th>
      <th>Code Value</th>
      <th>Icon</th>
      <th>Color (Light Mode)</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Info</td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">informational</code></td>
      <td>ℹ️ InfoIcon</td>
      <td>Blue</td>
      <td>General updates or logs</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Warning</td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">warning</code></td>
      <td>⚠️ AlertIcon</td>
      <td>Yellow</td>
      <td>Potential issues</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Error</td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">error</code></td>
      <td>❌ ErrorIcon</td>
      <td>Red</td>
      <td>Failures or critical problems</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Success</td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">success</code></td>
      <td>✅ InfoIcon</td>
      <td>Green</td>
      <td>Successfully completed actions</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<h4 id="status">Status</h4>
<p>Filter notifications based on whether they have been read. These statuses are defined in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">STATUS</code> and styled using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">STATUS_STYLE</code>.</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Status</th>
      <th>Code Value</th>
      <th>Icon</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Read</td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">read</code></td>
      <td>ReadIcon</td>
      <td>Notifications that have been opened</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Unread</td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">unread</code></td>
      <td>EnvelopeIcon</td>
      <td>New or untouched notifications</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<h3 id="understanding-notification-logos-and-icons">Understanding Notification Logos and Icons</h3>

<p>Meshery uses avatar icons to indicate who triggered a notification and what system was involved. These icons help users quickly understand the origin and nature of each event.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/avatar-icons.png">
  <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/avatar-icons.png" alt="Avatar Icons" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a></p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Icon Type</th>
      <th>Meaning</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Meshery logo only</td>
      <td>System-triggered event – initiated automatically by Meshery (e.g., syncing errors, import failures).</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>User avatar + Meshery logo</td>
      <td>User-triggered event – the user performed an action, and Meshery processed it (e.g., registering a Kubernetes context).</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>User avatar only (rare)</td>
      <td>User-triggered event with no system action involved.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p>These icons are generated dynamically using the event’s metadata:</p>
<ul>
  <li>If <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">user_id</code> is present → shows user avatar.</li>
  <li>If <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system_id</code> is present → shows Meshery logo.</li>
</ul>

<details close=""><summary>Visual Representation of System/User-triggered Notifications</summary>
  <br />

  <figure>
    <figcaption>
      1. 🟢 Meshery-only (System-triggered) Notification
      <a target="_blank" href="https://playground.meshery.io/extension/meshmap?mode=design&amp;design=a7310bb4-e642-4e4e-807a-dbb602228f07">
        (open in playground)
      </a>
    </figcaption>

  <script src="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/meshery-triggered.js" type="module"></script>

  <figure>
    <figcaption>
      2. 👤+🌐 User + Meshery (User-triggered) Notification
      <a target="_blank" href="https://playground.meshery.io/extension/meshmap?mode=design&amp;design=a96a3008-9c36-4862-b1e3-20cc2c35ca89">
        (open in playground)
      </a>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <div id="embedded-design-a96a3008-9c36-4862-b1e3-20cc2c35ca89" style="height:30rem;width:100%;"></div>
  <script src="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/user-triggered.js" type="module"></script>

</details>

<h3 id="notification-retention-and-visibility">Notification Retention and Visibility</h3>
<p><strong>How long are notifications stored?</strong></p>

<p>The duration for which notifications are retained is determined by the provider you are using (e.g., Meshery Cloud, local Meshery Server).</p>

<p><strong>What happens when retention ends?</strong></p>

<p>In Meshery Cloud, notifications are removed once the provider is updated, helping ensure the event stream reflects the most recent and relevant information.</p>

$(document).ready(function() {

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);

             })

        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })

          <h1>Infrastructure Management</h1>
           <h2 id="using-meshery-designs-to-manage-your-infrastructure">Using Meshery Designs to Manage Your Infrastructure</h2>

<p>Meshery is a versatile platform designed to streamline the lifecycle, configuration, and performance management of infrastructure across Kubernetes clusters.</p>

<h3 id="designs-in-meshery">Designs in Meshery</h3>

<p>Meshery employs the concept of <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a> as a fundamental construct for managing infrastructure. Designs provide a structured way to organize and deploy various components of your infrastructure. To do so, Meshery utilizes a declarative approach to infrastructure management, similar to Kubernetes manifests. Meshery Designs are written in YAML and are validated against a schema.</p>

<h4 id="importing-existing-infrastructure-and-applications">Importing Existing Infrastructure and Applications</h4>

<p>Meshery facilitates the import of infrastructure in multiple formats, including Kubernetes manifests, Helm Charts, and Docker Compose files. Import existing infrastructure definitions by directly from filesystem, via URL, or import directly from a GitHub repository.</p>

<ul>
  <li>Kubernetes Manifest</li>
  <li>Meshery Design</li>
  <li>Helm Charts</li>
  <li>Docker Compose</li>
</ul>

<p>See <a href="/v0.8/extensions/import-export-designs">Importing Designs</a> for more information.</p>

<details>
<summary>
<h3>Meshery Internals Provisioning Process</h3>
</summary>
<p>When a request is made to provision a design, it undergoes the following stages:</p>
<h4>1. Import of Referenced Designs</h4>
<p>A Design may reference any number of other Designs, in essence, a Design may import any number of other Designs.  As an editor of a Design, you can make reference to another Design, while following principles of reusing and DRY (Do Not Repeat Yourself). Any referenced Design will subsequently be imported during the provisioning moment. To reference another design, do so by adding the following annotation <pre>type: $(#use \&lt;url-of-remote-pattern\&gt;)</pre> in your Design file. The referenced design will be expanded from the source.</p>
<h4>2. Identification</h4>
<p>Meshery relies on components registered at boot time. Only registered models and components can be managed with Meshery. Currently, models from the ArtifactHub repository are supported.</p>
<h4>3. Validation</h4>
<p>Components in the design are validated against the schema, ensuring consistency, similar to Kubernetes object validation but tailored for Designs.</p>

<h4>4. Dependency Detection and Resolution</h4>
<p>Meshery identifies and resolves dependencies among components using a dynamic mechanism based on each component’s origin (also known as its <code>host</code> or <code>registrant</code>). Provisioning order is critical—circular dependencies will result in termination of the deployment.</p>

<p>Deployment Mechanism by Source:</p>

<ul>
  <li><b>Artifact Hub:</b> Uses Helm Go client for Kubernetes Operator and CRD deployment via <code>ApplyHelmChart()</code>.</li>
  <li><b>Kubernetes YAML:</b> Direct application with Kubernetes Go client (no auto-dependency handling).</li>
</ul>

<p>This behavior is determined by the component’s host type:</p>

<pre>
if connection.Kind == "artifacthub" ➜ Helm Go client used
if connection.Kind == "kubernetes" ➜ Kubernetes Go client used
</pre>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Implementation Detail</h4>
This logic is handled in the <code>NewDependencyHandler()</code> function, which selects the deployment method based on <code>connection.Kind</code>.
</div>


<h4>5. Provisioning</h4>
<p>A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) generated in the previous step is processed. Dependent components are processed sequentially, while others are processed in parallel. Meshery intelligently handles the deployment order to ensure successful deployment.</p>
</details>

<h3>Auto-Deployment of CRDs and Operators</h3>

<p>Meshery automates the deployment of Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) and operators based on the source from which a particular component was registered. By default, Meshery automatically deploys components that are sourced from Artifact Hub (utilizing Helm Charts). Support for OCI registries is expected in the near future.</p>

<details>
<summary><h4>Understanding CRDs and Why Deployment Order Matters</h4></summary>

<p><b>What is a CRD?</b></p>
<p>Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) extend Kubernetes to support new resource types (e.g., <code>VirtualService</code>, <code>Gateway</code>). A CRD must be installed <b>before</b> any resource of that type is deployed, or you’ll encounter errors like <i>“no matches for kind…”</i>.</p>

<p><b>Why does Meshery only auto-deploy CRDs for ArtifactHub?</b></p>
<p>Helm Charts (used by ArtifactHub) are bundled with CRDs and operators, making it safe for Meshery to auto-deploy them via Helm Go client.</p>

<p>In contrast, Kubernetes YAML files may be minimal or incomplete. Meshery cannot assume what dependencies you intended. Therefore, Meshery avoids auto-deployment to prevent accidental conflicts or errors.</p>

<p><b>User Responsibility (for non-ArtifactHub components):</b></p>
<p>If you use Kubernetes YAML, ensure that all required CRDs and operators are included. Meshery will apply the YAML as-is using the Kubernetes Go client, but will <b>not auto-deploy</b> missing dependencies for you.</p>

</details>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Upcoming Features</h4>
<p>Meshery is actively developing the ability to import custom models and components, expanding the platform's flexibility. Support for OCI registries is expected in the near future.</p><p><b>1. Custom Models and Components:</b> Import your own models for more flexibility.</p><p><b>2. OCI Registry Support:</b> In addition to ArtifactHub, OCI registries will be supported soon.</p>
</div>

$(document).ready(function() {

    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);

        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });

          <h1>Infrastructure Discovery</h1>
           <div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">MeshSync</h4>
Managed by the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/operator">Meshery Operator</a>, MeshSync is a custom Kubernetes controller that provides tiered discovery and continual synchronization with Meshery Server as to the state of the Kubernetes clusters and their workloads. Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/meshsync">MeshSync</a>.
</div>

<p>MeshSync is your tool for efficient management and synchronization of Kubernetes clusters! This user guide will walk you through how to establish a connection with any element that Meshery is able to connect to and manage. Use the MeshSync page to register connections, view connection metadata, and perform connectivity tests, as weel as to manage credentials and environments.</p>

<h2 id="meshsync-discovery">MeshSync Discovery</h2>

<p>MeshSync involves the discovery and registration of elements in your infrastructure. Follow these steps to seamlessly integrate and manage your connections:</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Discovered</strong>: Fill out the registration form, specifying metrics to listen to for Prometheus.</li>
  <li><strong>Register</strong>: Your object will now appear on the connection page.</li>
</ol>

<p>Tasks performed during registration:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Enrich connections with more information about your infrastructure.</li>
  <li>Offload fingerprinting process to MeshSync.</li>
  <li>Connect with KubeAPI for connections management.</li>
  <li>Handle curated list of connections (port, protocol, etc.).</li>
  <li>Display Meshery Models icons/colors for every discovered object with connection definitions pointing to components.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="meshery-server-database-updates">Meshery Server Database Updates</h3>

<p>Meshery Server writes updates from MeshSync to the server database:</p>

<p>Meshery uses the component’s Group, Version, Kind to perform the initial tier of fingerprinting.</p>

<h3 id="meshsync-endpoint">MeshSync Endpoint</h3>

<p>The Meshery Server endpoint performs a simple JOIN of GVKs to enrich responses with Component Metadata. Key points to note:</p>

<h2 id="connection-management">Connection Management</h2>

<h3 id="during-connection-registration">During Connection Registration</h3>

<p>Upon registration, the MeshSync object should have a status of “REGISTERED.” Follow these steps:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Create a new entry in the Connections table with either “REGISTERED” or “CONNECTED,” based on the Meshery Server’s ability to establish a connection.</li>
  <li>Use the Registration Modal to assign the connection to an environment.</li>
  <li>Confirm connection metadata details, including the assigned model and component.</li>
  <li>Perform a connectivity test to determine the status: “REGISTERED” (administratively connected) or “CONNECTED” (both administratively and actually connected).</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="registration-modal">Registration Modal</h3>

<p>The Registration Modal allows users to assign connections to environments, view connection metadata, and perform connectivity tests. Key features include:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Connectivity test to determine registration status.</li>
  <li>Identification of credentials to be used, with a selection based on CredentialDefinition for the ConnectionDefinition being registered.</li>
  <li>Future options to offer generic CredentialDefinitions for various authentication methods.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="credential-registration">Credential Registration</h3>

<p>During credential registration, users can assign credentials to one or more connections and perform ad hoc connectivity tests. UI buttons include “Test” and “Register.”</p>

<h2 id="connection-configuration">Connection Configuration</h2>

<p>The benefit of normalizing and extracting the status of a component as a direct property of the connection is to allow different systems to connect to the same component with different states. For example, multiple Meshery servers can connect to the same Kubernetes cluster, each having its own individual connection with a unique status.</p>

<p>Now that you are familiar with MeshSync and its powerful features, you are ready to streamline your Kubernetes cluster management.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Deploying Sample Applications</h1>
           <p>Meshery includes a few sample applications to help you explore cloud native infrastructure. Each is a collection of microservices for experimental purposes of learning about running workloads in Kubernetes clusters both on and off of cloud native infrastructure. When deploying a sample app onto your cloud native infrastructure, your sample application needs will need to be externaally exposed from the cluster, if you would like to access it externally. There are a myriad of ways to do this, specific to the infrastructure you are using.</p>

<p>A popular way of exposing your cluster is by using <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/">Ingress</a>, an API object that defines rules which allow external access to services in a cluster.</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/#the-ingress-resource">Set up Ingress</a></li>
  <li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-application-cluster/ingress-minikube/">Set up Ingress on Minikube</a></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="deploy-a-sample-app-on-meshery">Deploy a sample app on Meshery</h2>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>Go to the management page of any infrastructure and install any of its stable versions.
      <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-install.png"><img alt="Consul-install" style="width:500px;height:auto;display:flex;padding-top:10px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-install.png" /></a></p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Click (+) on <strong>Manage Sample Application Lifecycle</strong>. You will now be able to see a dropdown menu with the available sample applications.
      <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-sample-app.png"><img alt="ImageHub sample app" style="width:500px;height:auto;display:flex;padding-top:10px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-sample-app.png" /></a></p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Click on the sample application you want to deploy. This might take up to a minute. You will be notified when the sample application has been deployed.
      <a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-imagehub-success.png"><img alt="ImageHub deployed" style="width:500px;height:auto;display:flex;padding-top:10px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-imagehub-success.png" /></a></p>
  </li>
</ol>

<h3 id="bookinfo">BookInfo</h3>

<p>Originally built by Istio, BookInfo is a sample application which on deployment displays information about a book, similar to a single catalog entry of an online book store. Displayed on the page is a description of the book, book details (ISBN, number of pages, and so on), and a few book reviews. The application comprises of four microservices:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>productpage</strong>: The productpage microservice calls the details and reviews microservices to populate the page.</li>
  <li><strong>details</strong>: The details microservice contains book information.</li>
  <li><strong>reviews</strong>: The reviews microservice contains book reviews. It also calls the ratings microservice.</li>
  <li><strong>ratings</strong>: The ratings microservice contains book ranking information that accompanies a book review.</li>
</ul>

<p>Once BookInfo is deployed, you can use Meshery to apply custom configurations to control traffic, inject latency, perform context-based routing, and so on.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/bookinfo.png"><img alt="BookInfo sample app" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/bookinfo.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="emojivoto"><a href="https://github.com/BuoyantIO/emojivoto">Emojivoto</a></h3>

<p>Emojivoto is a microservice application, originally built by Linkerd that allows users to vote for their favorite emoji, and tracks votes received on a leaderboard. The application is composed of three microservices:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>emojivoto-web</strong>: Web frontend and REST API</li>
  <li><strong>emojivoto-emoji-svc</strong>: gRPC API for finding and listing emoji</li>
  <li><strong>emojivoto-voting-svc</strong>: gRPC API for voting and leaderboard</li>
</ul>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/emojivoto.png"><img alt="Emojivoto" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/emojivoto.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="imagehub">ImageHub</h3>

<p>Image Hub is a sample application for exploring WebAssembly modules used as Envoy filters. The application was originally written to run on Consul. However, it doesn’t have any dependency on Consul and can be deployed on any infrastructure. These modules can be used to implement multi-tenancy or to implement per user rate limiting in your application’s endpoints, without messing with your application infrastructure. </p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/imagehub-on-consul.png"><img alt="Imagehub-on-Consul" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/imagehub-on-consul.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="httpbin"><a href="https://httpbin.org">HTTPBin</a></h3>

<p>HttpBin is a simple HTTP request and response service that responds to many kinds of http/https requests including the standard http request methods (or verbs) used by REST.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/httpbin.png"><img alt="httpbin" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/httpbin.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="linkerd-books"><a href="https://github.com/BuoyantIO/booksapp">Linkerd Books</a></h3>

<p>Linkerd Books is a sample Ruby based application. It is designed to demonstrate the various value propositions, including debugging, observability, and monitoring of your infrastructure. It can be used to scope out your mesh’s efficiency and for debugging.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/linkerd-books.png"><img alt="Linkerd Books" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/linkerd-books.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="online-boutique"><a href="https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo">Online Boutique</a></h3>

<p>Online Boutique is a sample cloud-native application, originally built by Google. It comprises of 10 microservices and can be used to showcase and work with Kubernetes, Istio, gRPC and OpenCensus. On deployment, it runs a web-based e-commerce demo application, an example of which can be seen below:</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/online-boutique.png"><img alt="Online Boutique" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/sample-apps/online-boutique.png" /></a></p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });

<!-- <a href="http://idratherbewriting.com" class="noCrossRef productSubtitle"> Home </a> > <a class="noCrossRef productSubtitle" href="https://docs.meshery.io">Learn API Doc</a> > authenticate-with-meshery-via-cli -->

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Authenticating Meshery via CLI</h1>
           <p>To authenticate Meshery through <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code>, the Meshery CLI, you will use the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system login</code> command. On executing this command, you will be provided with a list of providers to choose from. You can then select a Provider of your choice to complete the authentication and authorization process.</p>

<p>As of this writing, you will be presented with two providers, <em>Meshery</em> and <em>None</em>.</p>
<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>Use the arrow keys to navigate: ↓ ↑ → ← 
? Select a Provider: 
  ▸ Meshery
    None
</code></pre></div></div>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p>Selecting <em>Meshery</em> will open a browser to complete the login and authentication process with Meshery Cloud. On successful authentication, you can close the window and return to the command prompt.</p>

    <p>Verify that an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">auth.json</code> file was created in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> folder in your home directory.</p>

    <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nb">ls</span> <span class="nt">-l</span> <span class="nv">$HOME</span>/.meshery/

total 12
<span class="nt">-rw-rw-r--</span> 1 ubuntu ubuntu  39 Dec 21 06:13 auth.json
<span class="nt">-rw-rw-r--</span> 1 ubuntu ubuntu 260 Dec 21 06:04 config.yaml
<span class="nt">-rw-rw-r--</span> 1 ubuntu ubuntu 988 Dec 21 06:04 meshery.yaml
</code></pre></div>    </div>

    <p><strong><em>The need for authentication to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Meshery</code> <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensibility/providers">provider</a> is to save your environment setup while also having persistent/steady sessions and to be able to retrieve performance test results.</em></strong></p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Selecting <em>None</em> will create an empty <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">auth.json</code> file. All your work remains local and ephemeral.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>If <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> is running in a system that does not have a browser, you can download an auth token file from your Meshery Cloud account and copy it into the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> folder in your home directory. The following steps show how you can generate and download a token:</p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>Navigate to <a href="https://cloud.meshery.io/security/tokens">https://cloud.meshery.io/security/tokens</a> and sign-in.
Ensure you are in the right organization and click <strong>Create</strong>.</p>

    <p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/token/create-token.png"><img alt="Create Token" src="/assets/img/token/create-token.png" /></a></p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Provide a token name and purpose. Click <strong>Create</strong> to generate.</p>

    <p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/token/generate-token.png"><img alt="Generate Token" src="/assets/img/token/generate-token.png" /></a></p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Click the <strong>Download</strong> icon to download the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">auth.json</code> file.</p>

    <p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/token/download-token.png"><img alt="Download Token" src="/assets/img/token/download-token.png" /></a></p>
  </li>
</ol>

<p>Then run <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check</code> to ensure you do not see an authentication error.</p>

<p>For an exhaustive list of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> commands and syntax, visit <a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> Command Reference</a>.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<!-- <a href="http://idratherbewriting.com" class="noCrossRef productSubtitle"> Home </a> > <a class="noCrossRef productSubtitle" href="https://docs.meshery.io">Learn API Doc</a> > configuring-autocompletion-for-mesheryctl -->

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Configuring Autocompletion for `mesheryctl`</h1>
           <p>If you would like to have <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> commands automatically completed for use as you use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code>, then use the following instructions to configure automatic completion within your environment.</p>

<h2 id="autocompletion-for-bash">Autocompletion for Bash</h2>

<h3 id="bash--32">bash &lt;= 3.2</h3>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">source /dev/stdin &lt;&lt;&lt; "$(mesheryctl completion bash)"</div></div>
 </pre>

<h3 id="bash--40">bash &gt;= 4.0</h3>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">source &lt;(mesheryctl completion bash)</div></div>
 </pre>

<h3 id="bash--32-on-macos">bash &lt;= 3.2 on MacOS</h3>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">brew install bash-completion # ensure you have bash-completion 1.3+
mesheryctl completion bash &gt; $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/mesheryctl</div></div>
 </pre>

<h3 id="bash--40-on-macos">bash &gt;= 4.0 on MacOS</h3>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">brew install bash-completion@2
mesheryctl completion bash &gt; $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/mesheryctl</div></div>
 </pre>

<h2 id="autocompletion-for-zsh">Autocompletion for zsh</h2>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">source &lt;(mesheryctl completion zsh)</div></div>
 </pre>
<p><br /></p>

<p>If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need to enable it. You can execute the following once:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">~/.zshrc &gt; echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit"</div></div>
 </pre>

<p><em>Note</em> : You might need to restart your shell for this setup to take effect.</p>

<h4 id="zsh-on-macos-and-oh-my-zsh">zsh on MacOS and Oh My zsh</h4>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">COMPLETION_DIR=$(echo $fpath | grep -o '[^ ]*completions' | grep -v cache) &amp;&amp; mkdir -p $COMPLETION_DIR &amp;&amp; mesheryctl completion zsh &gt; "${COMPLETION_DIR}/_mesheryctl"</div></div>
 </pre>

<h3 id="autocompletion-for-fish">Autocompletion for fish</h3>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl completion fish | source</div></div>
 </pre>
<p><br /></p>

<p>To load fish shell completions for each session, execute once:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl completion fish &gt; ~/.config/fish/completions/mesheryctl.fish</div></div>
 </pre>

<p>For an exhaustive list of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> commands and syntax:</p>

<ul>
  <li>See <a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> Command Reference</a>.</li>
</ul>

<p>Guides to using Meshery’s various features and components.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Running system checks using Meshery CLI</h1>
           <p>Meshery’s CLI, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code>, includes commands for verifying system readiness for a Meshery deployment and health checks to confirm the health of an existing Meshery deployment. Whether you have yet to deploy Meshery or have already deployed Meshery, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check</code> is a useful utility to ensure that your Meshery deployments are healthy.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system check</div></div>
</pre>
<p><br /></p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">Verify environment pre/post-deployment of Meshery.

Usage:
mesheryctl system check [flags]

Flags:
--adapter Check status of Meshery adapters
-h, --help help for check
--operator Check status of Meshery operators
--pre Verify environment readiness to deploy Meshery
--preflight Verify environment readiness to deploy Meshery

Global Flags:
--config string path to config file (default "/Users/navendu/.meshery/config.yaml")
-c, --context string (optional) temporarily change the current context.
-v, --verbose verbose output
-y, --yes (optional) assume yes for user interactive prompts.</div></div>
</pre>

<h2 id="deployment-checks">Deployment checks</h2>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check</code> command can run two types of system checks. A pre-deployment check which verifies the environment to deploy Meshery and a post-deployment check which runs validation checks on a running Meshery deployment.</p>

<h3 id="pre-deployment-checks">Pre-deployment checks</h3>

<p>Pre-deployment checks runs checks on the environment and verifies whether it is ready for deploying Meshery.</p>

<p>The following checks are done here:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Docker health checks: Checks for the availability of Docker and docker-compose in the user’s machine</li>
  <li>Kubernetes health checks: Checks for the availability of a Kubernetes cluster and checks if Meshery can initialize a Kubernetes client</li>
  <li>Kubernetes version checks: Checks if kubectl and the Kubernetes version are higher than the minimum supported versions</li>
</ul>

<p>Pre-deployment checks are run with the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--preflight</code> flag as shown below:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system check --preflight</div></div>
</pre>

<h3 id="post-deployment-checks">Post-deployment checks</h3>

<p>Post-deployment checks are run after deploying Meshery in the user’s environment. These checks ensure that the running deployment of Meshery and Meshery adapters are working as expected.</p>

<p>In addition to the pre-flight checks, the following checks are also run in this check:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Meshery version checks: Checks the version of Meshery server and CLI and shows if a new version is available</li>
  <li>Meshery Adapter health checks: Checks if all the specified adapters are deployed and reachable</li>
</ul>

<p>Post-deployment checks are run as shown below:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system check</div></div>
</pre>

<h2 id="additional-checks">Additional checks</h2>

<p>To check the status of the deployed adapters only, users can leverage the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--adapter</code> flag as shown below:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system check --adapter</div></div>
</pre>

<p>Users can also narrow down the tests to just check the status of the Meshery operator deployed on their Kubernetes cluster:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system check --operator</div></div>
</pre>

<h2 id="faq">FAQ</h2>

<h5 id="question-while-running-mesheryctl-system-check---preflight-it-says-i-didnt-install-kubernetes-but-i-have-docker-installed-and-the-test-returned-meshery-prerequisites-met-is-that-all-good">Question: While running <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check --preflight</code> it says I didn’t install Kubernetes, but I have Docker installed and the test returned “Meshery prerequisites met”. Is that all good?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>Yes, as long as you’ve Docker installed, it’s fine to run Meshery. But you will need a Kubernetes cluster to handle tasks such as deploying infrastructure and so on, if you want to do them via Meshery.</em></p>

<h5 id="question-i-ran-a-preflight-check-to-see-if-i-satisfy-all-requirements-for-meshery-in-my-system-it-returned-positive-results-but-i-couldnt-start-meshery-what-to-do">Question: I ran a preflight check to see if I satisfy all requirements for Meshery in my system. It returned positive results but I couldn’t start Meshery. What to do?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>Make sure if you’ve configured your system to run Meshery in smooth manner. For configuration, do check out the docs site and <a href="/v0.8/installation">this page</a> to see instructions related to the platform you use.</em></p>

<h5 id="question-do-i-need-a-kubernetes-cluster-or-will-a-docker-host-suffice-for-meshery-deployments">Question: Do I need a Kubernetes cluster or will a Docker host suffice for Meshery deployments?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>Meshery’s <a href="/v0.8/guides/performance-management/managing-performance">performance management</a> functionality does not require a Kubernetes cluster. The rest of Meshery’s functionality (e.g. cloud native management) does require a Kubernetes cluster.</em></p>

<h5 id="question-what-are-mesherys-production-deployment-requirements">Question: What are Meshery’s production deployment requirements?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>One or more Kubernetes clusters. A stateful set for Meshery Server in order to persist performance test results. See <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/issues/2451">#2451</a>.</em></p>

<h5 id="question-for-system-checks-do-i-need-any-add-ons-to-pass-the-check">Question: For system checks, do I need any add-ons to pass the check?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>Not necessary. Basic requirements are enough to pass the check.</em></p>

<h5 id="question-the-adapter-check-is-failing-it-returns-auth-token-not-found">Question: The Adapter check is failing, it returns “Auth token not found”.</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>You can log in to Meshery using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system login</code> which would generate an OAuth token. Once the OAuth token is generated, the check will start to function</em></p>

<h5 id="question-i-have-a-kubernetes-cluster-enabled-but-meshery-couldnt-reach-the-cluster-and-the-checks-are-failing-what-to-do">Question: I have a Kubernetes cluster enabled but Meshery couldn’t reach the cluster and the checks are failing! What to do?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>To resolve this error, you can upload your kubeconfig file in the Meshery UI under settings and Meshery will reconfigure to use your Kubernetes cluster.</em></p>

<h5 id="question-under-meshery-version-test-im-getting-an-error-like-cli-is-not-up-to-date-should-i-update-mesheryctl-often">Question: Under Meshery Version test, I’m getting an error like “CLI is not up-to-date”. Should I update mesheryctl often?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>Yes! You should update the mesheryctl often in order to run Meshery smoothly. The reason behind it is because not only the CLI is updated, but also the Meshery app. So it is advisable to update Meshery often.</em></p>

<h5 id="question-is-it-advisable-to-keep-meshery-in-sleep-mode-while-running-system-checks">Question: Is it advisable to keep Meshery in sleep mode while running system checks?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>Not necessary. It is good to keep Meshery up and running, else the system checks will fail to detect the Meshery version.</em></p>

<h5 id="question-what-is-the-minimum-version-of-k8s-cluster-and-kubectl-required-to-run-meshery">Question: What is the minimum version of k8s cluster and kubectl required to run Meshery?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>For Kubernetes, version &gt;=1.12.0 is recommended. For kubectl version &gt;=1.12 is recommended.</em></p>

<h5 id="question-in-the-meshery-adapter-section-of-check-i-could-see-only-some-meshery-adapters-up-and-running-and-not-all-is-this-fine">Question: In the “Meshery Adapter” section of check, I could see only some Meshery adapters up and running and not all. Is this fine?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>Not a problem, if you feel you need to have all mesh adapters to be up running, you can do so by creating a new context <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context create [context-name] --set</code> (if you voluntarily deleted mesh adapters in your current context)</em></p>

<h5 id="question-i-started-meshery-fresh-didnt-change-any-of-the-details-in-the-context-i-have-but-i-see-that-all-adapter-checks-are-failing-what-to-do">Question: I started Meshery fresh, didn’t change any of the details in the context I have. But I see that all adapter checks are failing. What to do?</h5>

<p><strong>Answer</strong>: <em>Configure Meshery to use on your Kubernetes cluster, then upload the kubeconfig file via Meshery UI to notify Meshery to use that cluster. If that didn’t work, feel free to <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/issues">open up an issue</a> in GitHub.</em></p>

<h3 id="suggested-reading">Suggested Reading</h3>

<p>For an exhaustive list of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> commands and syntax:</p>

<ul>
  <li>See <a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> Command Reference</a>.</li>
</ul>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>
