        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Mesheryctl system commands</h1>
           <p>Let’s get familiar with mesheryctl system commands. The syntax of the mesheryctl commands goes as follws : <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl &lt;Main_command&gt; &lt;Argument&gt; &lt;Flags&gt;</code></p>

<h2 id="main_command--system">Main_command : system</h2>
<h3 id="start">start</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system start</code> : This will initiate Meshery &amp; automatically open it in your default web browser.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/start.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/start.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system start --skip-browser</code> : It skips opening Meshery in your browser with the provided URL.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/skipbrowser.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/skipbrowser.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system start --skip-update</code> : It is used when you want to skip updating Meshery if an update is available.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/system update.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/system update.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system start --reset</code> : It resets your Meshery configuration file to its default configuration.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system start --platform string</code> : It allows you specify a platform for deploying Meshery.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/platform.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/platform.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="stop">stop</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system stop</code> : It stops Meshery resources &amp; delete its associated namespaces.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/stop.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/stop.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system stop --reset</code> : It stops Meshery and resets the Meshery configuration file to its default configuration.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/stop reset.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/stop reset.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system stop --keep-namespace</code> : It stops Meshery without deleting the associated namespaces.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/keep namespace.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/keep namespace.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system stop --force</code> : Force stops Meshery instead of gentle way. This is only used in emergency situations when <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system stop</code> can’t halt Meshery.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/force stop.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/force stop.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="update">update</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system update</code> : This updates Meshery itself, not the mesheryctl. Ensure Meshery is running when using this.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/system update.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/system update.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system update --skip-reset</code> : Skips the check for a new manifest file.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/update skip reset.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/update skip reset.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="reset">reset</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system reset</code> : Resets Meshery to its default configuration.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/reset.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/reset.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="restart">restart</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshryctl system restart</code> : Stops Meshery and then starts it again. Opens the website in your default browser.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/restart.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/restart.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="status">status</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system status</code> : Displays the status of Meshery components.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system status --verbose</code> : Provides additional data along with Meshery and its component status.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/system status.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/system status.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="dashboard">dashboard</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system dashboard</code> : Opens the Meshery dashboard in your default browser.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/system dahboard.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/system dahboard.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system dashboard --skip-browser</code> : Provides the link to the dashboard, allowing you to open it in any browser.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/dashboard skip.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/dashboard skip.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code> : If the current port is busy, it opens the dashboard on another port.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/portforward.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/portforward.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="login">login</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system login</code> : Authenticates you with your selected provider.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/system login.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/system login.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="check">check</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check</code> : Performs checks for both pre &amp; post mesh deployment scenarios on Meshery.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/system check.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/system check.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check --preflight</code> : Runs pre-deployment checks.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check --adapter</code> : Runs checks for a specific Mesh adapter.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check --adapters</code> : Runs checks for Meshery adapters</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check --components</code> : Runs checks for Meshery components</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system check --operator</code> : Runs checks for Meshery Operator</p>

<h2 id="main_command--system-channel">Main_command : system channel</h2>
<h3 id="channel">channel</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system channel set [stable|stable-version|edge|edge-version]</code> : Used to set the channel.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system channel switch [stable|stable-version|edge|edge-version]</code> : Used to switch between channels.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/channel set.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/channel set.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system channel view --all</code> : Displays all available channels.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system channel view</code> : Displays the current channel.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/channel view.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/channel view.png" /></a></p>

<h2 id="main_command--system-context">Main_command : system context</h2>
<h3 id="create">create</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context create 'context-name'</code> : Creates a new context with default parameters.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/context create.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/context create.png" /></a></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context create --component stringArray</code> : Specifies the component to be created in the context.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context create --platform string</code> : Specifies the platform.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context create --set</code> : Sets this  context as default context.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context create --url string</code> : Specifies the target URL.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/context flag.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/context flag.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="switch">switch</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context switch</code> : Easily switch between different contexts.</p>

<h3 id="list">list</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context list</code> : Lists all your available Meshery contexts.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/context list.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/context list.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="delete">delete</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context delete</code> : Delete context.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/context delete.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/context delete.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="view">view</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context view</code> : Display all your contexts with additional information.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/context view.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/context view.png" /></a></p>

<h2 id="main_command--system-provider">Main_command : system provider</h2>
<h3 id="switch-1">switch</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system provider switch</code> : Changes your provider</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/pro switch.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/pro switch.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="list-1">list</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system provider list</code> : Lists all available providers</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/pro list.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/pro list.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="set">set</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system provider set</code> : Set your provider</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/pro set.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/pro set.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="view-1">view</h3>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system provider view</code> : Lists your current context and provider</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/syscmd/pro view.png"><img alt="skip-browser" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/syscmd/pro view.png" /></a></p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Using Meshery CLI</h1>
           <p>Meshery’s command line interface is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code>. Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> to both manage the lifecyle of Meshery itself and to access and invoke any of Meshery’s application and cloud native management functions. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> commands can be categorized as follows:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> - Global overrides and flags</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl app</code> - Cloud Native Application Management</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl filter</code> - Cloud Native Filter Management</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl mesh</code> - Cloud Native Lifecycle &amp; Configuration Management</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl perf</code> - Cloud Native Performance Management</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl design</code> - Cloud Native Pattern Configuration &amp; Management</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system</code> - Meshery Lifecycle and Troubleshooting</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="configuring-meshery-deployments-with-meshconfig">Configuring Meshery Deployments with meshconfig</h2>

<p><em>Meshconfig</em> refers to a configuration file found at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">~/.meshery/config.yaml</code>. Your meshconfig file must contain one or more <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">contexts</code> in order for any <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system</code> command to work. Each context represents a Meshery deployment.</p>

<p>Each of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system</code> commands are used to control Meshery’s lifecycle like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system start</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">stop</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">status</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">reset</code> and so on.</p>

<h2 id="meshery-cli-faq">Meshery CLI FAQ</h2>

<h4 id="question-what-is-the-meshconfig">Question: What is the meshconfig?</h4>

<p>Like kubeconfig for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kubectl</code>, meshconfig is the name of your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> config file. You can find your meshconfig file in its default location of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">~/.meshery/config.yaml</code>. By default, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> will look to this location for your meshconfig. You can override the default location at anytime with the use of the global parameter, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--config &lt;my-other-meshconfig&gt;</code>.</p>

<h4 id="question-what-is-a-context">Question: What is a context?</h4>

<p>A meshconfig <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">context</code> represents a single Meshery deployment. Using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">context</code>s, you can configure different Meshery deployments with environment-specific settings and you can easily switching between your individual Meshery deployments by updating your current-context.</p>

<h4 id="question-why-are-contexts-necessary">Question: Why are contexts necessary?</h4>

<p>Many Meshery users have more than one Meshery deployment. Contexts allow you to deploy different versions of Meshery, update your release channel subscription settings, selectively install one or more Meshery Adapters, and so on. Contexts allow you to configure your individual Meshery deployments.</p>

<h4 id="question-what-is-current-context">Question: What is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">current-context</code>?</h4>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">current-context</code> identifies the Meshery deployment that when any <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> command is invoked will use the environment described in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">current-context</code>. You can switch between contexts. Only one context can be the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">current-context</code>.</p>

<h4 id="question-whats-the-difference-between-contexts-and-environments">Question: What’s the difference between contexts and environments?</h4>

<p>Contexts configure Meshery deployments (server, adapters, operator and so on), while environments define a collection of Kubernetes clusters and cloud native infrastructure under management in Meshery.</p>

<h4 id="question-what-does-the-default-meshconfig-look-like">Question: What does the default meshconfig look like?</h4>

<p>The following template is used to create a config file from scratch. Not all of the following variables are required to be included. Some of the variables may have a null value or may be excluded (e.g. “adapters”).</p>

<h4 id="question-what-is-the-importance-of-config-flag">Question: What is the importance of –config flag?</h4>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--config</code> flag is a global option that applies to all <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> commands. It allows you to specify the location of a custom meshconfig file, overriding the default configuration. This config file is used to set up the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> context, which defines the configuration for a particular Meshery deployment.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
contexts:
  [context1-name]:
    endpoint: [url to meshery server rest api]
    token: [name of token variable in this config file]
    platform: [type of platform: "docker" or "kubernetes"]
    # Future: specify type of kubernetes (e.g. eks)
    channel: [release channel: "stable", "stable-version", "edge", or "edge-version"]
    adapters: [collection of names of Meshery adapters:
        "istio","linkerd","consul","nginx-sm","tanzu-sm","cilium","app-mesh","traefik-mesh","nighthawk","kuma","osm","nsm"]
    version: [version of Meshery client "latest", "v0.8.132", ...]
    provider: [meshery's providers: "Meshery", "None", ...]
    # add ENVs here
    env:
      meshsync_deployment_mode: ["operator" or "embedded", defaults to "operator"]

  [context2-name]:
    endpoint: [url to meshery server rest api]
    token: [name of token variable in this config file]
    platform: [type of platform: "docker" or "kubernetes"]

current-context: [context name]

tokens:
  - name: [token1-name]
    location: [token-location]
  - name: [token2-name]
    value: [token-value]
    # Future: allow embedding of token certificate

</div></div>
</pre>
<p><br /></p>

<p>Try it out and see for yourself. Run <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context create test</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system context view test</code>.</p>

<h4 id="question-how-do-endpoints-work-in-meshconfig">Question: How do endpoints work in meshconfig?</h4>

<p>Endpoints specify the access URL for the Meshery UI, for a deployment. Endpoints are developed based on platform:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Docker: Docker users can specify the endpoint in the meshconfig. The port specified in this will be used to generate the endpoint. The endpoint is of the form <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">http://localhost:port</code>, where <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">port</code> is taken from the meshconfig.</li>
  <li>Kubernetes: Deployments with kubernetes as the platform have an endpoint generated by service discovery using the Kubernetes API. This endpoint overwrites the endpoint specified in the meshconfig.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="question-can-i-get-an-api-token-using-mesheryctl">Question: Can I get an API token using mesheryctl?</h4>

<p>Yes, if you need to establish a session with your Meshery Server, you can <a href="/v0.8/guides/mesheryctl/authenticate-with-meshery-via-cli">authenticate using mesheryctl</a>, using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system login</code>.</p>

<h2 id="advanced-installation">Advanced Installation</h2>

<p>Users can control the specific container image and tag (version) of Meshery that they would like to run by editing their local <em>~/.meshery/meshery.yaml</em> (a docker compose file).
Aligned with the Meshery container image, instead of leaving the implicit :stable-latest tag behind image: meshery/meshery, users will instead identify a specific image tag like so:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">
version: &#39;3&#39;
services:
  meshery:
    image: meshery/meshery:v0.5.0
    labels:
      - &quot;com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true&quot;</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="suggested-reading">Suggested Reading</h3>

<p>For an exhaustive list of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> commands and syntax:</p>

<ul>
  <li>See <a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> Command Reference</a>.</li>
</ul>

<p>Guides to using Meshery’s various features and components.</p>

## Installing `mesheryctl`

### Mac or Linux

Use your choice of homebrew or bash to install `mesheryctl`. You only need to use one.
### Homebrew

Install `mesheryctl` and run Meshery on Mac with Homebrew.

#### Installing with Homebrew

To install `mesheryctl`, execute the following commands:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 brew install mesheryctl
 mesheryctl system start
 </div></div>
 </pre>

**Upgrading with Homebrew**

To upgrade `mesheryctl`, execute the following command:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 brew upgrade mesheryctl
 </div></div>
 </pre>

#### Bash

**Installing with Bash**

Install `mesheryctl` and run Meshery on Mac or Linux with this script:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 curl -L https://meshery.io/install | bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>

**Upgrading with Bash**

Upgrade `mesheryctl` and run Meshery on Mac or Linux with this script:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 curl -L https://meshery.io/install | bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>

## Windows

### Installing the `mesheryctl` binary

Download and unzip `mesheryctl` from the [Meshery releases](https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/) page. Add `mesheryctl` to your PATH for ease of use. Then, execute:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 ./mesheryctl system start
 </div></div>
 </pre>

### Scoop

Use [Scoop](https://scoop.sh) to install Meshery on your Windows machine.

**Installing with Scoop**

Add the Meshery Scoop Bucket and install:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 scoop bucket add mesheryctl https://github.com/meshery/scoop-bucket.git
 scoop install mesheryctl
 </div></div>
 </pre>

**Upgrading with Scoop**

To upgrade `mesheryctl`, execute the following command:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 scoop update mesheryctl
 </div></div>
 </pre>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Interpreting Performance Test Results</h1>
           <p>Once a performance tests and run, it’s disco analysis is performed and test results persisted. Results or downloadable and persisted in the <a href="https://smp-spec.io/">Cloud Native Performance</a> format.</p>

<h2 id="graphical-view">Graphical View</h2>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/dashboard.png" /></p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/chart.png" /></p>

<h2 id="tests">Tests</h2>

<p>For the best experience, you should compare between two or more tests of similar configuration. Tests that are configured with a high degree of variance (e.g., one test ran for a duration of 5 minutes, while another test ran for a duration of 1 hour) will produce comparisons that are more difficult to extrapolate insights from.</p>

<p>Latency and throughput are the two most significantly examined signals.</p>

<p>Meshery will use different algorithms to calculate results depending upon which load generator was used to run the test.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Managing Performance</h1>
           <p>Key to the efficient operation of any infrastructure is the measurement and management of it’s performance.</p>

<h2 id="performance-profiles">Performance Profiles</h2>

<p>Performance Profile is a new and improved way to save performance test configurations, schedule performance tests, etc. Meshery Performance Profiles offers the following features:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Saving Test Configurations</li>
  <li>Create schedules for running tests automatically.</li>
  <li>Meshery offers UI for describing the schedules which are as powerful as CRON but without the hassle of remembering its syntax!</li>
  <li>All the tests performed are under Profiles which has multiple advantages like:
    <ul>
      <li>Access test results ran under a certain profiles at one place.</li>
      <li>If running ad-hoc tests, user can anytime come back and rename the performance profiles for re-use.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<h2 id="load-generators">Load Generators</h2>

<p>Meshery provides users with a choice about the kind of load generator they prefer to use for a given performance test. Users may set their configure based on their own preference of load generator different from that of the default load generator.</p>

<p>Meshery supports the following load generators and is <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensibility">extendible</a> to support others:</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="#fortio">fortio</a></li>
  <li><a href="#wrk2">wrk2</a></li>
  <li><a href="#nighthawk">Nighthawk</a></li>
</ul>

<h3 id="fortio">fortio</h3>

<p>Fortio is a fast, small (3Mb docker image, minimal dependencies),
reusable, embeddable go library as well as a command line tool and server process,
the server includes a simple web UI and graphical representation of the results
(both a single latency graph and a multiple results comparative min, max, avg, qps and percentiles graphs).</p>

<h3 id="wrk2">wrk2</h3>

<p>It is a modern HTTP benchmarking tool capable of generating significant load when run on a single multi-core CPU. It combines a multithreaded design with scalable event notification systems such as epoll and kqueue.</p>

<h3 id="nighthawk">Nighthawk</h3>

<p>NightHawk is an L7 (HTTP/HTTPS/HTTP2) performance characterization tool. It currently offers:</p>

<ul>
  <li>A load testing client which supports HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over HTTP and HTTPS. (HTTPS certificates are not yet validated).</li>
  <li>A simple test server which is capable of generating dynamic response sizes, as well as inject delays.</li>
  <li>A binary to transform nighthawk output to well-known formats, allowing integration with other systems and dashboards.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="configuring-performance-testing-settings">Configuring performance testing settings</h2>

<p>Meshery provides a highly configurable set of load profiles with various, tuneable facets, including support for generating TCP, gRPC, and HTTP load with optional configuration of the performance test’s:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Duration</li>
  <li>Concurrent Threads</li>
  <li>Concurrent Generators</li>
  <li>Load Generator Type</li>
  <li>Custom HTTP Headers</li>
</ul>

<p>See <a href="https://smp-spec.io">Cloud Native Performance</a> for a full description of the different types of performance tests that Meshery provides.</p>

<h3 id="using-performance-test-profiles">Using Performance Test Profiles</h3>

<p>As Meshery user you can customize and save your load test configuration in the form of a Performance Test Profile. Using Performance Test Profiles, you can return to Meshery to run the same set of customized tests again and again, tracking variations in performance overtime.</p>

<h3 id="comparing-test-results-and-different-configurations">Comparing Test Results and Different Configurations</h3>

<p>Meshery users can easily compare the difference in request performance (latency and throughput) between independent performance tests. Statistical analysis is run upon finalization of every performance test and presented in the form of a histogram with latency buckets.</p>

<h2 id="kubernetes-cluster-and-workload-metrics">Kubernetes Cluster and Workload Metrics</h2>

<p>Meshery provides performance test results alongside environment metrics, including control and data plane metrics as well as cluster node resource metrics, so that operators may easily understand the overhead of their control plane and data plane in context of the overhead incurred on nodes within the cluster.</p>

<h3 id="grafana-and-meshery">Grafana and Meshery</h3>

<p>Connect Meshery to your existing Grafana instance. Meshery will auto-import the boards of your choosing:</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/meshery-and-grafana.png">
    <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/meshery-and-grafana.png" style="width: 52%" />
</a></p>

<h3 id="connecting-to-grafana">Connecting to Grafana</h3>

<p>If you have an API key configured to restrict access to your Grafana boards, you will need to enter the API key when establishing Meshery’s connection to Grafana. You may also set up a <a href="https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/http_api/dashboard/#create-update-dashboard">Grafana board</a> and then set up an API key:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Import Grafana boards
    <ul>
      <li>Import existing Grafana boards via API</li>
      <li>Import custom Grafana board via yaml</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Configure graph panel preferences</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="prometheus-and-meshery">Prometheus and Meshery</h3>

<p>Meshery allows users to connect to one or more Prometheus instances in order to gather telemetric data (in the form of metrics). These metrics may pertain to Kubernetes and applications or any other metric that Prometheus has collected.</p>

<p>Once you have connected Meshery to your Prometheus deployment(s), you may perform ad-hoc connectivity tests to verify communication between Meshery and Prometheus.</p>

$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Using Metrics in Meshery</h1>
           <h2 id="connect-and-use-metrics-in-meshery">Connect and use metrics in Meshery</h2>

<p>Meshery provides performance reports, including performance test results, node resource metrics etc. so that operators may easily understand the overhead of their cloud native infrastructure control plane and data plane in context of the overhead incurred on nodes running within the cluster. In order to generate performance test reports of infrastructure and their workloads, Meshery uses Grafana and/or Prometheus as visualization and metrics systems, respectively. This guide outlines the requirements necessary for Meshery to connect to these systems. The steps may vary depending upon the infrastructure and its configuration.</p>

<p>In order to pull in these environment metrics, you can also manually configure Meshery to connect with your existing Grafana and/or Prometheus instances through the Meshery dashboard. Once they have been loaded and are displayed on the screen, you may also perform an <em>ad-hoc</em> test to check Meshery’s connection status.</p>

<main>
  
  <input id="tab1" type="radio" name="tabs" checked="" />
  <label for="tab1">Prometheus Metrics</label>
    
  <input id="tab2" type="radio" name="tabs" />
  <label for="tab2">Grafana Charts</label>
    
  <input id="tab3" type="radio" name="tabs" />
  <label for="tab3">Static Boards</label>
    
  <input id="tab4" type="radio" name="tabs" />
  <label for="tab4">Dynamic Boards</label>
    
  <section class="tabbed" id="content1">
    <p>User needs to set the Prometheus URL and API key to create and query boards.</p>
    <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/PrometheusCharts.svg" alt="Prometheus Metrics in Meshery" />

  </section>
    
  <section class="tabbed" id="content2">
    <p>User needs to set the Grafana URL and API key to create and query boards.</p>
    <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/GrafanaBoards.svg" alt="Grafana Charts in Meshery" />

  </section>
    
  <section class="tabbed" id="content3">
    <p>
      Static Boards capture the standard performance metrics included in every Meshery performance test irrespective of which load generator is used. A set calculations are made using statistical analysis of the metrics gathered in the static boards. Static Boards Queries Prometheus SDK directly.
    </p>
  </section>
    
  <section class="tabbed" id="content4">
    <p>
      Dynamic Boards can be generated from Prometheus or Grafana. These boards are defined by the user. Grafana SDK is used for these boards.
    </p>

  </section>
    
</main>

<!-- ## Tutorial Guide

Connect Meshery to your Grafana and Prometheus instances to enable enhanced service mesh performance management. Deploy a service mesh and any available sample application

Retrieve the IP address of your Minikube cluster by executing:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 minikube ip
 172.17.0.2
 </div></div>
 </pre>

* Set up Grafana and/or Prometheus:
1. [Connect Meshery to metric systems](#connect-meshery-to-metric-systems)
2. [Connect Meshery to metric systems using Minikube](#Connect-Meshery-to-metric-systems-using-Minikube)

* Expose the service metric ports - The service ports of Grafana and Prometheus need to be exposed in order for Meshery to connect to and interact with these visualizations and metrics systems.
* Access the port assigned to the metric service
* [Run Performance tests](#run-performance-tests)


### **Connect Meshery to metric systems**

#### 1. Using kubectl, edit the Grafana and Prometheus services in the *Istio-system* namespace:

```sh
kubectl edit svc grafana -n istio-system
```

#### 2. Change specification type

By default, the service specification types, like Grafana is configured to `ClusterIP`. You can change it to `NodePort` by executing:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 kubectl patch svc prometheus -p '{"spec": {"type": "NodePort"}}' -n istio-system
 </div></div>
 </pre>

#### 3. Get the newly assigned port for your chosen service

Run:
```
kubectl get svc grafana -n istio-system
```

Example output:
```
NAME      TYPE       CLUSTER-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)          AGE
grafana   NodePort   10.100.67.144   <none>        3000:30188/TCP   3d11h
```

#### 4. Access the service port

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 http://172.17.0.2:30822
 </div></div>
 </pre>

###### 2. Expose the service

By default, the service specification types, like Prometheus, Grafana, and the `productpage`, are configured to **ClusterIP**. You can change it to **NodePort** by replacing *service spec type* with the spec you wish to run and executing:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 kubectl patch svc grafana -p '{"spec": {"type": "NodePort"}}' -n istio-system
 </div></div>
 </pre>

### **Expose Grafana service**

* Get the NodePort of Grafana service using below command

```
kubectl describe services grafana -n istio-system|grep NodePort

o/p:NodePort:  http  32130/TCP
```

* Find the Grafana endpoint

The Grafana endpoint will be *http://$MINIKUBE_IP:NODE_PORT*

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 http://172.17.0.2:32130
 </div></div>
 </pre>

<a href="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-metrics/grafana-server-settings.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-metrics/grafana-server-settings.png" />
</a>

### **Expose Prometheus service**

Meshery allows you to expose Prometheus as a service with a single click. You can do this:
- [Through the Meshery UI](#meshery-ui)
- Alternatively, you can also attempt [Manual Integration](#manual-steps)

#### **Meshery UI**

Meshery auto-discovers all Prometheus instances available on your local system and will offer you a list of options to choose from. You can select the Prometheus Server that you wish to employ.


<a href="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-metrics/prometheus-settings.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-metrics/prometheus-settings.png" />
</a>

Meshery also provides you the option of simply pasting in your Prometheus queries:

- Navigate to the management page for Istio on the Meshery UI
- Click on <i class="fas fa-caret-right fa-lg"></i>, located under **Apply Custom Configuration**
- Paste in your Prometherus query. Click on <i class="fas fa-caret-right fa-lg"></i>

<a href="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-metrics/prometheus-query.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-metrics/prometheus-query.png" />
</a>

#### **Manual Steps**

* Get the NodePort of Prometheus service by executing:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 kubectl patch svc grafana -p '{"spec": {"type": "NodePort"}}' -n book-info
 </div></div>
 </pre>

* Find the Prometheus endpoint

The Prometheus endpoint will be *http://$MINIKUBE_IP:NODE_PORT*

```
http://172.17.0.2:30822
```

#### **Expose Istio BookInfo sample app `productpage` service**

* Get the NodePort of `productpage` service by executing:

```
kubectl describe services productpage -n book-info|grep NodePort

NodePort:  http  30535/TCP
```

* Find the `productpage` endpoint

The `productpage` endpoint will be http://$MINIKUBE_IP:NODE_PORT

 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 http://172.17.0.2:30535/productpage
 </div></div>
 </pre>

#### **Run Performance Tests**

After successfully setting up a connection between your metric service and Meshery, you may proceed to run performance tests by navigating to the Performance Test tab on Meshery:

<a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/performance-meshery.png"><img style="width:450px;padding-top:5px;" src="/assets/img/performance-management/performance-meshery.png" /></a>

**Run Test Results**

<a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/meshery-and-grafana.png"><img style="width:450px;padding-top:5px;" src="/assets/img/performance-management/meshery-and-grafana.png" /></a> -->

$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Performance Management with Meshery</h1>
           <p>This guide walks through running performance benchmarks using Meshery. Users can either use the Meshery UI, the CLI, mesheryctl or run performance tests in their CI/CD pipelines using the Meshery GitHub Action.</p>

<h2 id="installing-meshery">Installing Meshery</h2>

<p>Install and login to Meshery to start running performance benchmarks. See <a href="/v0.8/installation">Installation</a> documentation for detailed steps on how to install Meshery.</p>

<p><em>Meshery dashboard</em></p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/smi/dashboard.png"><img alt="Meshery Dashboard" src="/assets/img/smi/dashboard.png" /></a></p>

<p>If you are looking to run performance benchmarks on cloud native infrastructur, you can use Meshery’s cloud native infrastructurelifecycle management capabilities to deploy all kinds of cloud native infrastructure on Kubernets. With Meshery’s performance benchmarking feature, you can also deploy you application off the mesh and compare the performance and determine the overhead when the app runs on the mesh.</p>

<p>Next, we navigate to the main Performance Testing dashboard. See <a href="/v0.8/guides/performance-management/managing-performance">Performance Management</a> to learn more about performance profiles, load generators, Kubernetes cluster, and all kinds of cloud native infrastructure metrics.</p>

<h2 id="running-performance-benchmarks-through-meshery-ui">Running Performance Benchmarks Through Meshery UI</h2>

<p>Meshery UI provides an easy-to-use interface in which users can create performance profiles to run repeated tests with similar configuration and can also even schedule performance tests to be run at particular times through the calendar.</p>

<p>On the navigation menu, click on performance.</p>

<p>This will open the performance management dashboard as shown below.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/performance-management-dashboard.png"><img alt="Performance Management Dashboard" src="/assets/img/performance-management/performance-management-dashboard.png" /></a></p>

<p><em>Performance Management Dashboard</em></p>

<p>To create a performance profile, click on “Manage Profiles” and then select “+ Add Performance Profile”.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/performance-profiles.png"><img alt="Performance Profiles" src="/assets/img/performance-management/performance-profiles.png" /></a></p>

<p><em>Performance Profiles</em></p>

<p>This will open up a popup window where you can fill out the test configuration for running your benchmarks.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/running-tests.png"><img alt="Performance Test Configuration" src="/assets/img/performance-management/running-tests.png" /></a></p>

<p><em>Configuring a Performance Test</em></p>

<p>You can now save the profile and run the test. The test will continue to run in the background even if you close the popup.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/running-tests-spinner.png"><img alt="Running a performance test" src="/assets/img/performance-management/running-tests-spinner.png" /></a></p>

<p>Once the test is done, you would be able to see the results of the test below.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/result-chart.png"><img alt="Running a performance test" src="/assets/img/performance-management/result-chart.png" /></a></p>

<p><em>Performance Test Results</em></p>

<p>You can then go back to your performance profile and get these results anytime.</p>

<p>You can also compare different test results in Meshery and draw insights. For example, you can run this test with your application running on different cloud native infrastructure and check which performs better.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/comparison-table.png"><img alt="Comparing Test Results" src="/assets/img/performance-management/comparison-table.png" /></a></p>

<p><em>Selecting multiple test results</em></p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/performance-management/comparison.png"><img alt="Comparing Test Results" src="/assets/img/performance-management/comparison.png" /></a></p>

<p><em>Comparing multiple test results</em></p>

<h2 id="running-performance-benchmarks-through-mesheryctl">Running Performance Benchmarks Through mesheryctl</h2>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl perf</code> subcommand provides the performance management features of Meshery in the CLI.</p>

<p>To run a performance test based on a performance profile, run:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl perf apply Istio Performance Test
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>You can also use flags to configure your performance test. For example:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl perf apply istio-soak-test --concurrent-requests 1 --duration 15s --load-generator nighthawk --mesh istio --url http://localhost:2323
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>mesheryctl also supports test configurations written in SMP compatible format as shown below:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>test:
  smp_version: v0.0.1
  name: Istio Performance Test
  labels: {}
  clients:
    - internal: false
      load_generator: fortio
      protocol: 1
      connections: 2
      rps: 10
      headers: {}
      cookies: {}
      body: ''
      content_type: ''
      endpoint_urls:
        - 'http://localhost:2323/productpage'
  duration: '30m'
mesh:
  type: 3
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>And then you can pass this file to mesheryctl as:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl perf apply -f perf-config.yaml
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>You can also override the configuration passed in the file with flags like shown below:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl perf apply -f perf-config.yaml --url http://localhost:2323/productpage?u=test --load-generator nighthawk --qps 5
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="running-performance-benchmarks-in-your-pipelines">Running Performance Benchmarks in your Pipelines</h2>

<p>Meshery also has a <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-smp-action">meshery-smp-action</a> which is a GitHub action that can be used to run performance tests in your CI/CD pipelines.</p>

<p>Download the token from the Meshery Dashboard by clicking on the profile icon on the top-right corner.</p>

<p><em>Downloading the token</em></p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/smi/download-token.png"><img alt="SMI Conformance Test Results" src="/assets/img/smi/download-token.png" /></a></p>

<p>You can use this token to authenticate the instance of Meshery running in your CI/CD workflow.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Using the token in GitHub workflows</h4>
You can use the <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/encrypted-secrets">secrets feature in GitHub</a> to store the token.
</div>

<p>The action can be used by defining your test configuration in a performance profile in Meshery or by writing your test configuration in <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-smp-action#smp-compatible-test-configuration-file">SMP compatible format</a>.</p>

<p>The action can then be configured as shown below:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>name: Meshery SMP Action
on:
  push:
    branches:
      'master'

jobs:
  performance-test:
    name: Performance Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v2
        with:
          ref: 'perf'

      - name: Deploy k8s-minikube
        uses: manusa/actions-setup-minikube@v2.4.1
        with:
          minikube version: 'v1.21.0'
          kubernetes version: 'v1.20.7'
          driver: docker

      - name: Run Performance Test
        uses: Meshery/meshery-smp-action@master
        with:
          provider_token: $
          platform: docker
          profile_name: soak-test
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>More configuration details of the action can be found <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-smp-action/blob/master/action.yml">here</a>.</p>

<p>See <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-smp-action#sample-configuration">sample configurations</a> for more workflow examples using this action.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Troubleshooting Extensions for Local Development</h1>
           <p>If you’ve set up your local Meshery development environment and an extension isn’t showing up, this guide is here to help. Before you start debugging, the most important first step is to understand the <strong>type</strong> of the component you are troubleshooting.</p>

<p>Meshery has different types of extensions that integrate in different ways. This means their failure modes and troubleshooting methods are also very different.</p>

<h2 id="step-1-locate-the-extensions-repository">Step 1: Locate the Extension’s Repository</h2>

<p>Most Meshery extensions are open source and their repositories can be found in the <a href="https://github.com/orgs/meshery-extensions/repositories?type=all">meshery-extensions GitHub organization</a>. Your first step is to find the specific repository for the extension you are troubleshooting.</p>

<p>If you can find the repository and it is public, proceed with the steps for <a href="#loosely-coupled-extensions">Loosely-Coupled Extensions</a>.</p>

<p>If you cannot find the repository or it is private, the issue is likely related to a dependency mismatch, a common challenge with <a href="#tightly-coupled-extensions">Tightly-Coupled Extensions</a>.</p>

<h2 id="step-2-follow-the-troubleshooting-path">Step 2: Follow the Troubleshooting Path</h2>

<h3 id="loosely-coupled-extensions">Loosely-Coupled Extensions</h3>

<p>These extensions communicate with Meshery Server through standard APIs. Issues are typically easier to diagnose.</p>
<ul>
  <li>Example: <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a> like the <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-istio">meshery-istio</a> adapter.</li>
  <li>Common Issues: Networking problems, port conflicts, or component-specific errors.</li>
  <li>Debugging Steps: Use standard tools like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">docker ps</code> to check if the container is running and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">docker logs &lt;container-id&gt;</code> to inspect its logs for errors.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="tightly-coupled-extensions">Tightly-Coupled Extensions</h3>

<p>These extensions are highly sensitive to their environment because they require exact package versions to match the Meshery Server.</p>
<ul>
  <li>Example: <a href="https://.new/">Meshery </a>, a visual designer for Kubernetes and cloud native applications.</li>
</ul>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Resolving Dependency Mismatches</h4>
Problems with tightly-coupled extensions are often **not traditional code bugs** but rather version conflicts between the extension and your local Meshery environment.
</div>

<h4 id="why-you-cant-fix-this-locally">Why you can’t fix this locally</h4>

<p>You don’t have permission to access the private code repository. This means:</p>
<ul>
  <li>You <strong>cannot build the extension from source</strong></li>
  <li>Your only option is using a <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-extensions-packages">pre-built package</a></li>
</ul>

<h4 id="the-dependency-mismatch-problem">The dependency mismatch problem</h4>

<p>Tightly-coupled plugins require <strong>exact package matches</strong> between the extension and your Meshery server. When using pre-built packages:</p>
<ul>
  <li>They might work if dependencies happen to match your local environment</li>
  <li>Any update to your Meshery server will likely break compatibility</li>
  <li>Failures often occur without clear error messages</li>
</ul>

<blockquote>
  <p>Without source access, these dependency issues are practically unresolvable.</p>
</blockquote>

<h4 id="next-steps">Next Steps</h4>

<p>Given that you cannot build the extension from source, a solution typically requires seeking assistance.</p>

<p>While you can attempt to experiment by manually testing different versions of packages from the <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-extensions-packages">meshery-extensions-packages</a> repository, this trial-and-error method is not guaranteed to work.</p>

<p>The most reliable path forward is to:</p>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Seek assistance:</strong> Ask for guidance in the <a href="/v0.8/project/community">Meshery community</a>.</li>
</ul>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>
